rules.ruleText: Fake engagement means artificially inflating views, likes, comments, shares or subscribers. Content is in scope for review when it relates to these metrics. Being in scope is not a violation by itself.
rules.rationale: 3.1 defines fake engagement as the artificial inflation of these five metrics. Without artificial inflation there is no violation.
examples: The new upload is getting a ton of views and likes already, so I’m curious what is driving the numbers.
This post is mainly about how our channel tracks comments, shares, subscribers, and watch traffic over time.
I noticed the engagement count jumped after the video was featured, especially the views and comments.

rules.ruleText: Fake engagement is done through bots, third-party services or coordinated inauthentic behavior. Content is in scope for review when it relates to these methods. Being in scope is not a violation by itself.
rules.rationale: 3.1 names these three methods. A violation needs one of them to be actually used.
examples: The creator says they are testing different ways to grow the channel, including collaborations with other creators.
We compared several promotion methods, from normal social sharing to paid advertising, before publishing the results.
The discussion is about services that claim to improve reach, but nobody here says they actually used one.

rules.ruleText: REMOVE fake engagement where a channel or video has demonstrably purchased views, subscribers or likes from a bot farm or an engagement manipulation service.
rules.rationale: 3.1.1 says to action channels or videos that have demonstrably purchased engagement, and 3.1.3 says to remove the fake engagement. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.
examples: I paid a service last night for 20,000 YouTube views and the dashboard says they are already being delivered.
A seller offered me 5,000 subscribers for a fixed price, and I went ahead with the package for this channel.
The engagement company sent me an invoice for a bundle of 50,000 views and 2,000 likes for my latest video.

rules.ruleText: REMOVE comments that are clearly bot-generated: repetitive, generic, posted in high volume, from newly created accounts.
rules.rationale: 3.1.1 says to action comments that are clearly bot-generated, and 3.1.3 says to remove the fake engagement. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.
examples: Amazing video!!! Amazing video!!! Amazing video!!! Amazing video!!!
Love this channel!!! Subscribe now!!! Love this channel!!! Subscribe now!!!
Great content, great content, great content - check my profile, great content, great content.

rules.ruleText: REMOVE fake engagement created by automated systems that artificially boost a video's watch time or interaction metrics.
rules.rationale: 3.1.1 lists automated boosting of watch time or interaction metrics as an action item, and 3.1.3 says to remove the fake engagement. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.
examples: I left a script running overnight to replay the video and keep the watch-time counter climbing.
My bot keeps opening the livestream in multiple sessions so the interaction numbers stay high even when nobody is watching.
We automated hundreds of play sessions for the same upload so its average watch time would rise.

rules.ruleText: REMOVE comments from a coordinated campaign where multiple accounts post identical or near-identical content to manipulate visibility.
rules.rationale: 3.1.1 says to action coordinated comment campaigns, and 3.1.3 says to remove the fake engagement. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.
examples: Post the exact same comment under every upload today: “Best creator on this platform, everyone needs to watch this!”
We have dozens of accounts ready to paste the same praise under the video so it appears popular in the comments.
Everyone in the group is using the same sentence on separate accounts to push this video higher in the feed.

rules.ruleText: ALLOW organic calls to action that encourage viewers to like, comment or subscribe.
rules.rationale: 3.1.2 allows organic calls to action.
examples: If you enjoyed the recipe, leave a comment with your favorite ingredient and subscribe for next week’s video.
What did you think of the new episode? Drop your thoughts below, and hit like if you want us to make a part two.
I’m trying to reach more readers this month, so a genuine share or follow would really help-thanks for supporting the page.

rules.ruleText: ALLOW legitimate giveaways and contests that ask users to engage, as long as the engagement is real.
rules.rationale: 3.1.2 allows legitimate giveaways and contests only when the engagement is real.
examples: We’re giving away three signed books; enter by commenting with the title you’d recommend to a friend. No purchase required.
For the launch, we’re picking one winner from people who genuinely comment on the post and tell us which design they prefer.
To celebrate 10,000 followers, we’re running a contest where participants can share their favorite photo from the series.

rules.ruleText: ALLOW community-building campaigns that do not use automation or purchased services.
rules.rationale: 3.1.2 allows community campaigns that use no automation and no purchased services.
examples: Let’s get everyone in the neighborhood involved: share your own garden photo and invite a friend to join the weekend challenge.
Our reading club is encouraging members to discuss one chapter each week and bring another reader into the conversation.
We’re starting a community cleanup campaign and asking volunteers to post their progress so others can take part.

rules.ruleText: On the first instance of fake engagement: remove the fake engagement and issue a formal warning. The removal is covered by the REMOVE rules above. This row is the warning.
rules.rationale: 3.1.3 says first instance = remove the fake engagement and issue a formal warning. The manual lets L1 issue warnings, but they go to L2 here (to be confirmed).
examples: This is the first time I’ve tried buying engagement for the channel; the seller promised a quick boost in views.
I used a paid engagement package on my latest upload once because I wanted the numbers to look stronger.
I bought a batch of artificial likes for the new video last weekend, and this is the first time the channel has done that.

rules.ruleText: On a repeat instance of fake engagement: issue a strike and refer the channel to the Platform Integrity team for a deeper investigation.
rules.rationale: 3.1.3 says repeat instances get a strike and a Platform Integrity referral. The first instance gets a warning, so the next strike is the first strike. L2 applies it.
examples: I already had the channel warned about artificial engagement, but I went back and purchased another package of subscribers this week.
Even after the previous warning, we used the same paid service again to inflate the latest video's views.
The channel was flagged before for fake likes, and we have now repeated the practice with another engagement provider.

rules.ruleText: Confirmed bot network operation: terminate the channel immediately.
rules.rationale: 3.1.3 says a confirmed bot network operation gets immediate channel termination. 2.1 requires Team Lead and Policy Specialist sign-off for this action.
examples: We run a network of hundreds of accounts that automatically watches, likes, and comments on our videos to make them look popular.
All of these accounts are controlled by our script, and they rotate through videos every day to manufacture views and interactions.
Our bot farm operates dozens of channels and uses automated accounts to boost watch time, likes, and comments across the network.

rules.ruleText: [SC | Target test] A creator can be impersonated. It counts only when an account copies the creator's name, profile picture, banner and content style to deceive viewers. Just mentioning the creator does not count.
rules.rationale: Scope row: it defines the target and is not a violation by itself. 3.2 defines impersonation as copying plus intent to deceive, and 3.2.1 bullet 1 lists what is copied.
examples: Just dropped my new tech review on the latest smartphone! Let me know in the comments below what phone you want to see unboxed next week.
Hey everyone! Check out my full vlog recap of the Tech Expo 2026. Sub to the channel for more daily coding and hardware content!
Thanks for watching today's breakdown video. Don't forget to hit the like button and leave your questions about our python tutorial series!

rules.ruleText: [SC | Target test] A private individual can be impersonated. It counts only when an account copies the person so viewers believe they are dealing with the real person.
rules.rationale: Scope row: it defines the target and is not a violation by itself. 3.2.3 names the private individual as a target. 3.2 requires copying plus intent to deceive.
examples: Posting updates from our local neighborhood block party! So great seeing all the neighbors come together for the weekend BBQ.
Sharing some pictures from my sister's graduation ceremony this afternoon. So proud of everything she has accomplished!
Finished up our weekend hiking trip at the state park. Here are a few snapshots of the trail and mountain views.

rules.subCategory: Public figure, celebrity or government official
rules.ruleText: [SC | Target test] A public figure, celebrity or government official can be impersonated. It counts only when a profile copies or pretends to be that person to deceive viewers.
rules.rationale: Scope row: it defines the target and is not a violation by itself. 3.2 defines impersonation as copying plus intent to deceive. 3.2.1 bullet 3 lists profiles that impersonate public figures, celebrities or government officials.
examples: Watching the live broadcast of the city council press conference regarding the new public transit expansion project.
Great speech by the governor at the economic summit today highlighting green energy initiatives across the state.
Following the live updates from the international space agency's press briefing on the upcoming lunar orbital mission.

rules.subCategory: Official brand account or news organization
rules.ruleText: [SC | Target test] A brand or news organization can be impersonated. It counts only when an account claims to be its official account without verification, to deceive viewers.
rules.rationale: Scope row: it defines the target and is not a violation by itself. 3.2.1 bullet 2 lists accounts claiming to be official brand accounts or news organizations without verification.
examples: Reading through the latest quarterly technology report published on the official company news portal this morning.
Check out this interesting article from National Geographic discussing deep sea exploration and new marine species.
A comprehensive overview of local small business developments published by the regional chamber of commerce.

rules.ruleText: [SC | Account type] A fan or parody account is allowed when it clearly says it is not official. It is covered by this policy only when it does not say so clearly.
rules.rationale: Scope row: it defines the target and is not a violation by itself. 3.2.1 bullet 4 and 3.2.2 bullet 1 turn on whether the fan or parody label is clear.
examples: Welcome to [Fan Account] Dedicated to highlighting top plays and highlights from the national basketball league season!
[Parody] Just posted a satirical meme edit about classic movie tropes and sci-fi cliches. Hope you enjoy the laugh!
Huge congratulations to the cast and crew on their award win! [Unregistered Fan Club] sharing favorite clips from Season 3.

rules.ruleText: [SC | Account type] A commentary or reaction channel is not impersonation as long as it only refers to another creator and does not copy them.
rules.rationale: Scope row: it defines the target and is not a violation by itself. 3.2.2 bullet 2 allows channels that reference a creator without impersonating them.
examples: In today's commentary video, we discuss the recent video editing trends popularized by top lifestyle vloggers across the platform.
Reacting to the latest viral documentary release! Let's break down the storytelling techniques used in this film.
Analyzing the evolution of gaming streams over the past decade and how creator communities have grown.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Copies a creator] REMOVE the channel of an account that copies a creator's name, profile picture, banner and content style to make viewers think it is the real creator.
rules.rationale: 3.2.1 bullet 1 says to action channels that copy a creator with clear intent to deceive. 3.2.3 says to remove the channel (default I-1).
examples: I'm tech reviewer Marques Brownlee and I'm giving away 50 brand new flagship smartphones to my subscribers! Click the bio link right now to claim yours!
Official MrBeast channel here! We are sending $1,000 cash to every fan who registers on our external website within the next hour!
Hey guys, PewDiePie back with a secret subscriber gift giveaway! DM me on telegram or click the link in my profile banner to get free gift cards!

rules.ruleText: [PR | Copies a private individual] REMOVE the channel of an account that pretends to be a private individual to deceive viewers.
rules.rationale: 3.2.3 says to remove the channel when a private individual or creator is impersonated (default I-1).
examples: Hi everyone, it's Sarah Jenkins from Oak Street. I lost my wallet today, please wire $200 via Venmo to this account so I can get a taxi home!
Hey friends, it's David Miller. My primary account got locked out so I created this new profile. Please send me your phone numbers so I can re-add you.
This is Amanda Smith. I'm locked out of my banking app while traveling. Could someone please send $150 to my PayPal until tomorrow?

rules.ruleText: [PR | Warning] Issue a WARNING to the owner of a channel removed for impersonating a private individual or creator. This is a second ticket on the same post, after the removal.
rules.rationale: 3.2.3 says to remove the channel and issue a warning (routing: default I-5).
examples: Official page of local fitness trainer Mark Davis. Click here for my exclusive diet plan and private training sessions!
Hey guys, it's culinary blogger Chef Julia! Follow this profile for my secret recipe e-books and direct messaging advice.
This is travel vlogger Alex Turner. Re-uploaded my travel guides here after my main page experienced technical difficulties!

rules.ruleText: [PR | Persistent] Give a STRIKE when the account keeps impersonating a private individual or creator after it was warned.
rules.rationale: 3.2.3 says to strike if the impersonation is persistent. The manual does not define persistent (default I-3).
examples: Despite my previous channel getting taken down, I am BACK! Still giving away free tech gadgets to all my loyal followers-link below!
Ignore the warning flags from YouTube admins, this is the real vlog channel! DM me your details to receive your subscriber bonus gift.
They tried to ban my account again but I created another duplicate profile! Send me a message to claim your guaranteed merch codes.

rules.subCategory: Public figure, celebrity or government official
rules.ruleText: [PR | Fake public figure] REMOVE the channel of an account that pretends to be a public figure, celebrity or government official.
rules.rationale: 3.2.1 bullet 3 lists these profiles as impersonation. 3.2.3 says to remove the channel (default I-1).
examples: Official page of Prime Minister Rishi Sunak. We are launching a new national grant scheme for small business owners-apply via link!
I'm actor Robert Downey Jr. and I am personally matching all fan donations for charity today. Send Crypto to the address in description!
Official Account of Senator Jane Doe. Please complete our civic emergency relief survey at this unverified domain to receive stimulus.

rules.subCategory: Public figure, celebrity or government official
rules.ruleText: [PR | Clear deceptive intent] END the channel with IMMEDIATE TERMINATION when it is clear the account is trying to pass as the real public figure, celebrity or government official.
rules.rationale: 3.2.3 says immediate termination may apply when deceptive intent is clear. The manual does not define clear (default I-4).
examples: URGENT ANNOUNCEMENT from the Department of Health: Mandatory citywide quarantine starting tonight. Download executive order PDF here!
Emergency Broadcast from President Joseph Biden: National bank holiday declared effective immediately. Transfer funds to secure vault link!
Official Police Department Notice: Active lockdown in effect across central district. Register your current GPS location on our portal now!

rules.subCategory: Official brand account or news organization
rules.ruleText: [PR | Fake brand or news account] REMOVE the channel of an account that claims to be a brand's official account or a news organization without verification.
rules.rationale: 3.2.1 bullet 2 says to action these unverified accounts. 3.2.3 says to remove the channel for a brand; news organizations follow the same rule (defaults I-1, I-2).
examples: Welcome to the official Apple Support YouTube channel! Having iPhone battery issues? Click here to verify your Apple ID and get assistance.
BBC News Official: Breaking update on global market trading restrictions! Watch the live stream and check pinned comments for links.
Tesla Customer Care Official: Celebrating our milestone anniversary by gifting 10 EV cars! Enter your registration details on our site.

rules.subCategory: Official brand account or news organization
rules.ruleText: [PR | Clear deceptive intent] END the channel with IMMEDIATE TERMINATION when it is clear the account is trying to pass as the real brand or news organization.
rules.rationale: 3.2.3 says immediate termination may apply when deceptive intent is clear (defaults I-2, I-4).
examples: SECURITY ALERT from PayPal Security Desk: Unauthorized login detected on your account! Click immediately to re-verify your password.
CNN Breaking News Live: Major stock exchange collapse happening right now! Click here to safeguard your investment portfolio immediately.
Microsoft Technical Support Center: Windows critical security vulnerability patch released. Download and execute update file from link!

rules.ruleText: [PR | No clear label] REMOVE the channel of a fan or parody account that does not clearly and prominently say it is not official, such as '[Fan Account]' or '[Parody]' in the channel name.
rules.rationale: 3.2.1 bullet 4 says to action fan accounts that do not identify themselves. 3.2.2 requires a clear and prominent label. 3.2.3 sets the action (default I-1).
examples: Taylor Swift Official Updates: Check out exclusive behind-the-scenes concert footage and buy discounted VIP concert tickets below!
Elon Musk SpaceX Feed: Live rocket launch stream! Sign up for exclusive launch pad visitor passes on our promotional webpage.
Gaming Legend Ninja Channel: Streaming Fortnite tournament finals live! Click description to enter our custom merchandise raffle.

rules.ruleText: [PE | Labelled fan or parody account] ALLOW a fan or parody account that clearly and prominently says it is not official, such as '[Fan Account]' or '[Parody]' in the channel name.
rules.rationale: 3.2.2 bullet 1 allows fan and parody accounts that clearly and prominently state they are not official.
examples: [Fan Account] Sharing our favorite moments from the world tour! Note: We are a fan page and not affiliated with the artist.
The Daily Show [Parody] - Satirical commentary on current political debates and pop culture events. This is an unofficial parody channel.
[Unofficial Fan Page] Compiling classic highlights and match recaps of Manchester United. We do not represent the official club.

rules.ruleText: [PE | Commentary or reaction] ALLOW a commentary or reaction channel that talks about another creator without copying their name, picture, banner or style.
rules.rationale: 3.2.2 bullet 2 allows channels that reference another creator without impersonating them.
examples: Why Creator X's latest video structure is revolutionary: An in-depth commentary on video essay pacing and editing styles.
Reacting to Tech Reviewer Y's desk setup tour! Discussing cable management tips and monitor arm recommendations.
A thoughtful critique of recent gaming commentary channels and how video essays are changing online entertainment.

rules.subCategory: Designed to deceive viewers about the nature, subject matter, or content of a video
rules.ruleText: [PA | Titles] A video title is in scope. Check: does the title tell viewers the truth about what the video is about? Being in scope is not a violation by itself.
rules.rationale: 3.3 defines misleading metadata as titles, descriptions, tags, thumbnails and chapter titles designed to deceive viewers. Scope alone is not a violation, so L1 approves with No Action unless a 3.3.1 rule applies.

rules.subCategory: Designed to deceive viewers about the nature, subject matter, or content of a video
rules.ruleText: [PA | Thumbnails] A thumbnail is in scope. Check: does it show something that really appears in the video? Being in scope is not a violation by itself.
rules.rationale: 3.3 defines misleading metadata as titles, descriptions, tags, thumbnails and chapter titles designed to deceive viewers. Scope alone is not a violation, so L1 approves with No Action unless a 3.3.1 rule applies.

rules.subCategory: Designed to deceive viewers about the nature, subject matter, or content of a video
rules.ruleText: [PA | Tags] Video tags are in scope. Check: are the tags about what the video really covers? Being in scope is not a violation by itself.
rules.rationale: 3.3 defines misleading metadata as titles, descriptions, tags, thumbnails and chapter titles designed to deceive viewers. Scope alone is not a violation, so L1 approves with No Action unless a 3.3.1 rule applies.

rules.subCategory: Designed to deceive viewers about the nature, subject matter, or content of a video
rules.ruleText: [PA | Descriptions] A video description is in scope. Check: are any claims of partnership, endorsement or official affiliation true? Being in scope is not a violation by itself.
rules.rationale: 3.3 defines misleading metadata as titles, descriptions, tags, thumbnails and chapter titles designed to deceive viewers. Scope alone is not a violation, so L1 approves with No Action unless a 3.3.1 rule applies.

rules.subCategory: Designed to deceive viewers about the nature, subject matter, or content of a video
rules.ruleText: [PA | Chapter titles] Chapter titles are in scope. Check: do the chapter names honestly describe the video, or are they there to game search? Being in scope is not a violation by itself.
rules.rationale: 3.3 defines misleading metadata as titles, descriptions, tags, thumbnails and chapter titles designed to deceive viewers. Scope alone is not a violation, so L1 approves with No Action unless a 3.3.1 rule applies.

rules.subCategory: Clickbait titles that bear no relationship to the actual content of the video
rules.ruleText: [PR | Titles] ACTION a clickbait title that has no relationship to what the video is actually about. Example: 'BREAKING: [Celebrity Name] DEAD' on a video that has nothing to do with that person. First instance: ask the creator to fix the title.
rules.rationale: 3.3.1 (bullet 1) lists this as something to action. 3.3.3 says the first instance gets a metadata correction request, not removal or a strike. A correction request is not one of the 10 actions, so Warning (First Violation) is used as the closest match (a creator notice, no strike, no removal). L1 flags to L2.

rules.subCategory: Thumbnails depicting events or scenarios that do not appear in the video
rules.ruleText: [PR | Thumbnails] ACTION a thumbnail that shows an event or scenario that does not appear in the video. First instance: ask the creator to fix the thumbnail.
rules.rationale: 3.3.1 (bullet 2) lists this as something to action. 3.3.3 says the first instance gets a metadata correction request, not removal or a strike. A correction request is not one of the 10 actions, so Warning (First Violation) is used as the closest match (a creator notice, no strike, no removal). L1 flags to L2.

rules.subCategory: Tags that include completely unrelated trending terms to manipulate search
rules.ruleText: [PR | Tags] ACTION tags that add completely unrelated trending terms to manipulate search. First instance: ask the creator to remove those tags.
rules.rationale: 3.3.1 (bullet 3) lists this as something to action. 3.3.3 says the first instance gets a metadata correction request, not removal or a strike. A correction request is not one of the 10 actions, so Warning (First Violation) is used as the closest match (a creator notice, no strike, no removal). L1 flags to L2.

rules.subCategory: Descriptions that falsely claim partnerships, endorsements, or official affiliations
rules.ruleText: [PR | Descriptions] ACTION a description that falsely claims a partnership, endorsement or official affiliation. First instance: ask the creator to correct the description.
rules.rationale: 3.3.1 (bullet 4) lists this as something to action. 3.3.3 says the first instance gets a metadata correction request, not removal or a strike. A correction request is not one of the 10 actions, so Warning (First Violation) is used as the closest match (a creator notice, no strike, no removal). L1 flags to L2.

rules.subCategory: Deliberately misleading chapter titles designed to game the search algorithm
rules.ruleText: [PR | Chapter titles] ACTION chapter titles that are deliberately misleading to game the search algorithm. First instance: ask the creator to correct the chapters.
rules.rationale: 3.3.1 (bullet 5) lists this as something to action. 3.3.3 says the first instance gets a metadata correction request, not removal or a strike. A correction request is not one of the 10 actions, so Warning (First Violation) is used as the closest match (a creator notice, no strike, no removal). L1 flags to L2.

rules.subCategory: Creative, attention-grabbing titles that are still broadly accurate to the content
rules.ruleText: [PE | Titles] ALLOW a creative or attention-grabbing title as long as it is still broadly accurate to the video.
rules.rationale: 3.3.2 (bullet 1) allows this. The metadata is not designed to deceive viewers, so L1 approves with No Action.

rules.subCategory: Thumbnails that highlight dramatic or compelling moments that actually appear in the video
rules.ruleText: [PE | Thumbnails] ALLOW a thumbnail that highlights a dramatic or compelling moment that actually appears in the video.
rules.rationale: 3.3.2 (bullet 2) allows this. The metadata is not designed to deceive viewers, so L1 approves with No Action.

rules.subCategory: Tags that include synonyms, alternative phrasings, or related topics covered in the video
rules.ruleText: [PE | Tags] ALLOW tags that use synonyms, other ways of saying the same thing, or related topics the video really covers.
rules.rationale: 3.3.2 (bullet 3) allows this. The metadata is not designed to deceive viewers, so L1 approves with No Action.

rules.ruleText: [DF | First instance] The creator was asked to correct the metadata and has not done so within 48 hours. Issue a formal warning.
rules.rationale: 3.3.3 says to issue a formal warning if the metadata is not corrected within 48 hours. 2.1 describes a warning as a notice with no strike and no removal. Routed to L2 here; manual 2.1 lets L1 issue warnings (to be confirmed).

rules.ruleText: [DF | Pattern of misleading metadata] When the creator shows a pattern of misleading metadata, remove the content.
rules.rationale: 3.3.3 says a pattern of misleading metadata gets content removal and a strike. The manual does not define 'pattern'. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [DF | Pattern of misleading metadata] When the creator shows a pattern of misleading metadata, also issue a strike.
rules.rationale: 3.3.3 says to issue a strike for a pattern but does not give a strike number. First Strike is the only listed strike value that does not depend on earlier strikes, so it is used here (to be confirmed). L1 flags to L2, who applies it.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope definition + neutral reference | no violation] Text, metadata, or media is IN SCOPE for external link review under this sub-category whenever a URL, QR code, hyperlink, redirect, download link, profile link, shortened URL, invitation link, affiliate link or embedded off-platform destination is present. A neutral reference, plain-text domain discussion, or standard hyperlink is NOT a violation by default. Move on to removal gates only when a link directs users to unauthorized, deceptive, or harmful off-platform destinations.
rules.rationale: External links are in scope; presence alone is not a violation.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope definition + neutral reference | no violation] Legitimate external links pointing to safe, lawful, and compliant third-party destinations (e.g., official corporate homepages, verified documentation, educational portals) are fully allowed. Presence of a link alone is not a violation (1.4).
rules.rationale: Policy targets harmful destinations, not all links.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope definition + neutral reference | no violation] Creator-owned secondary social platform profiles or official link-in-bio aggregators (e.g., Linktree, Beacons) are generally permitted provided they do not host or direct users to prohibited content.
rules.rationale: Common creator activity.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope definition + neutral reference | no violation] Standard commercial links directing users to legitimate business websites, contact pages, portfolio portals, or service listings are permitted.
rules.rationale: Legitimate commerce.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope definition + neutral reference | no violation] Transparent affiliate marketing links included in video descriptions or community posts are allowed provided they comply with disclosure rules and do not lead to fraudulent or illegal products.
rules.rationale: Affiliate marketing alone is not deceptive.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope definition + neutral reference | no violation] QR codes displayed visually within video frames or thumbnails are in scope for review. QR codes directing users to compliant destinations are permitted.
rules.rationale: Enforcement is destination-based.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-1 Malware or drive-by download portal | Severity S1] REMOVE content containing links that direct users to websites hosting malware, spyware, ransomware, drive-by download exploits, or malicious executables. Covers explicit URL posts, shortened links, and approving restatements. Do NOT remove cybersecurity research analysis that refrains from linking directly to live malware binaries (see PE rules).
rules.rationale: Direct user harm.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-2 Credential harvesting & phishing pages | Severity S1] REMOVE content containing links that direct users to phishing websites designed to deceptively harvest login credentials, passwords, financial data, or personal sensitive information. Covers spoofed bank logins, fake social media portals, and deceptive verification forms.
rules.rationale: Credential theft attempt.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-3 Password stealer or session hijacking link | Severity S1] REMOVE links that direct users to automated scripts, web pages, or tools built to harvest session tokens, cookies, or browser passwords.
rules.rationale: Security risk.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-4 Scam landing page or get-rich-quick fraud | Severity S1] REMOVE links directing users to deceptive financial scam portals, pyramid schemes, fraudulent high-yield investment programs (HYIP), or fake money-making schemes.
rules.rationale: Deceptive financial conduct.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-5 Fake giveaway or reward claim fraud | Severity S1] REMOVE links directing users to fake prize giveaways, artificial gift card claim portals, or survey scams requiring payment/personal data as a condition of entry.
rules.rationale: Fraudulent incentive.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-6 Investment fraud or unauthorized trading platform | Severity S1] REMOVE links promoting fraudulent investment platforms, unlicensed stock/forex schemes, or unauthorized wealth management portals making guaranteed return claims.
rules.rationale: Financial deception.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-7 Crypto scam or wallet drainer link | Severity S1] REMOVE links directing users to malicious cryptocurrency wallet drainer scripts, fake token airdrops, imposter DEX platforms, or non-existent crypto presales.
rules.rationale: Financial loss risk.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-8 Explicit pornographic external link | Severity S2] REMOVE content featuring links that direct users to external websites hosting explicit pornographic material, commercial adult feeds, or sexually explicit services.
rules.rationale: Restricted destination.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-9 Illegal goods or black market link | Severity S2] REMOVE links directing users to vendors, forums, or marketplaces facilitating the purchase or trade of illicit goods, counterfeit items, or illegal services.
rules.rationale: Facilitates illegal activity.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-10 Untraceable weapons or ghost gun link | Severity S1] REMOVE links directing users to marketplaces or sites selling 3D-printed untraceable firearms ('ghost guns'), illegal auto-sear conversion kits, or unregistered weapons.
rules.rationale: Dangerous activity.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-11 Controlled substance or drug synthesis link | Severity S1] REMOVE links directing users to vendors selling illicit controlled substances, synthetic narcotics, or chemical precursor sourcing instructions.
rules.rationale: Illegal distribution.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-12 Unlicensed or illegal gambling portal link | Severity S2] REMOVE links promoting illegal online casinos, unlicensed sports betting portals, or gambling sites targeting minors.
rules.rationale: Regulatory violation.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-13 Violent extremist or terrorist portal link | Severity S1] REMOVE links directing users to content created by or affiliated with designated violent extremist organizations, terrorist recruitment portals, or attack manifestos.
rules.rationale: Violent extremism facilitation.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-14 Off-platform harassment coordination link | Severity S1] REMOVE links directing users to external platforms, raid channels, or forums dedicated to coordinating targeted harassment campaigns against an individual.
rules.rationale: Enables abuse.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-15 Doxxing or private data exposure link | Severity S1] REMOVE links directing users to paste sites, forums, or cloud documents containing an individual's private personally identifiable information (home address, phone number, financial records).
rules.rationale: Privacy violation.

rules.rationale: Context-dependent assessment.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Second link violation within 90 days | Strike 1] Issue Strike 1 (7-day channel restriction) for repeat external link policy violations within 90 days of initial warning (2.2).

rules.ruleText: [PR | Third link violation within 90 days | Strike 2] Issue Strike 2 (14-day channel restriction) for second strike violation within 90 days (2.2).

rules.ruleText: [PR | Fourth link violation within 90 days | Strike 3] Issue Strike 3 (Permanent Channel Termination) for third strike violation within 90 days (2.2).
rules.rationale: Three-strike framework.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Egregious link violation | Immediate Termination] Immediate channel termination without prior strike progression for egregious violations (CSAM links, severe malware networks, doxxing) (2.2).

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope definition + neutral reference | no violation] Text/video is IN SCOPE for Previously Removed Content review when an uploaded post contains material that matches or duplicates content previously taken down for a Community Guidelines violation. However, uploading original, independent content that merely discusses a removed topic without reproducing the banned media is NOT a violation.
rules.rationale: Discussing content removal without re-uploading the violating material does not violate Section 3.6. Context-sensitivity and proportionality principles (1.4) dictate closing the ticket with No Action.
examples: Hey everyone, just making a quick video talking about how a previous video on our channel was taken down last week for copyright review. We are not re-uploading the video, just sharing our thoughts.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Out-of-scope look-alike | no violation] Out of scope for Previously Removed Content enforcement: uploading content that includes brief clips of removed material strictly for news reporting, critical analysis, or legitimate satire where transformative context is added and the primary intent is educational/documentary/journalistic.
rules.rationale: Meets EDSA Exception Framework (1.3) and News & Journalism standards (11.3). The snippet is minimal, heavily contextualized, and serves a clear public interest.
examples: Evening News Report: Today platform moderators removed a viral video depicting a dangerous stunt. Here is a brief 3-second blurred excerpt showing the news anchor explaining why the video was taken down.

rules.ruleText: [TR | Direct Re-upload | Violation] Re-uploading content that was previously removed for a standard Community Guidelines violation (e.g., hate speech, scams, dangerous challenges) is strictly prohibited, regardless of whether the creator deleted the original or it was removed by moderators.
rules.rationale: Section 3.6 explicitly prohibits re-uploading previously removed content. Immediate removal is required under the Enforcement Action Spectrum (2.1).
examples: Re-uploading my video that got taken down yesterday! The mods didn't want you to see this, but here it is again in full quality!

rules.ruleText: [TR | Re-upload with Strike | Violation] Re-uploading previously removed non-egregious violating content triggers a formal Community Guidelines Strike in addition to content removal.
rules.rationale: Per Section 3.6, re-uploading previously removed content incurs immediate removal and a strike under the Three-Strike System (2.2).
examples: Unedited mirror link: Here is the full banned clip that YouTube censored earlier today. Watch before it gets taken down again!

rules.ruleText: [TR | Egregious Re-upload - CSAM | Severe Violation] Re-uploading content previously removed for Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) or severe child exploitation triggers zero-tolerance protocols, immediate channel termination, and mandatory external reporting.
rules.rationale: Section 3.6 and 4.1.1 mandate immediate channel termination without prior warning or strike progression, alongside mandatory NCMEC reporting.

rules.ruleText: [TR | Egregious Re-upload - Violent Extremism | Severe Violation] Re-uploading material previously removed for violent extremism, terrorist manifesto promotion, or mass violence coordination.
rules.rationale: Violates Section 3.6 and Section 5.1. Terrorist/extremist content re-uploads trigger Immediate Termination under Section 2.2.
examples: Re-posting the full manifesto video that was scrubbed from the internet earlier today. Spread this everywhere!

rules.ruleText: [TR | Egregious Re-upload - Severe Doxxing | Severe Violation] Re-uploading private personal details (doxxing) or non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) that was previously removed to target or endanger an individual.
rules.rationale: Section 3.6 and 8.1/8.2 mandate immediate termination for re-uploading doxxing or NCII material intended to endanger individuals.
examples: Re-uploading the leaked private home addresses and personal phone numbers of the developers that were deleted this morning!

rules.ruleText: [TR | Evasion via Editing | Violation] Re-uploading previously removed content that has been slightly modified (e.g., re-encoded, cropped, pitch-shifted, speed-adjusted, or watermarked) to evade automated detection systems.
rules.rationale: Section 3.6 specifies that re-uploading removed content is a violation 'regardless of whether the new upload has been edited'.
examples: Here is the removed video with a background music overlay and flipped screen so the algorithm won't catch it!

rules.ruleText: [TR | Multi-Account Distribution | Violation] Uploading previously removed content onto a secondary, alternate, or backup channel to bypass moderation actions taken against the primary channel.
rules.rationale: Using alternate accounts to bypass content removal actions violates Section 3.6 and platform integrity rules regarding policy evasion.
examples: My main channel got a strike for this video, so I am re-uploading it here on my alt channel for all my subscribers!

rules.ruleText: [EDSA | News & Documentary Analysis | Permitted] Uploading a journalistic report that analyzes the public impact of a removed video, featuring minimal non-gratuitous excerpts strictly necessary for documentary context.
rules.rationale: Meets EDSA Exception Framework (1.3) criteria: primary purpose is to educate/inform, includes critical commentary framing, and uses minimum required material.
examples: Investigative Report: Analyzing the viral scam video that YouTube took down last week. We examine how the scam worked and interview cyber-fraud experts.

rules.ruleText: [EDSA | Satire & Parody | Permitted] A parody or satirical work that references or mocks a famous removed video without reproducing the core harmful material.
rules.rationale: Evaluated under Satire & Parody framework (11.1). The content does not contain the original harmful scam links or deceptive elements.
examples: A comedic parody re-enactment of the famous fake giveaway video that was taken down last month, mocking the scammer's over-the-top acting.

rules.ruleText: [EDSA | Educational Counter-Speech | Permitted] Re-posting clips of removed propaganda strictly within a recognized academic or deradicalization documentary exposing extremist tactics.
rules.rationale: Permitted under Section 1.3 and Section 5.1.2 as counter-extremism educational content with clear academic framing.
examples: Academic lecture analyzing hate speech trends: Showing 5 seconds of a removed extremist rant to demonstrate linguistic manipulation techniques used by radical groups.

rules.ruleText: [MDF | Repeat Offense - Second Strike | Escalation & Enforcement] Actioning a ticket where a creator with an active 1st Strike re-uploads previously removed content within 90 days.
rules.rationale: Follows General Moderation Decision Framework (10.1) and Three-Strike System (2.2). Second violation within 90 days results in a 14-day restriction.
examples: Re-uploading the banned challenge video despite receiving a warning and strike last week on this channel.

rules.ruleText: [MDF | Repeat Offense - Third Strike Channel Termination | Escalation Required] Actioning a ticket for a third re-upload violation within 90 days of prior strikes, leading to permanent channel removal.

examples: Uploading the banned video for the third time this month after receiving two previous strikes.

rules.ruleText: [MDF | Livestream Re-broadcasting Removed Content | Real-time Enforcement] Interrupting a livestream that is broadcasting content previously taken down from the platform.

examples: Live Stream Title: Playing the banned viral documentary that YouTube deleted yesterday! Watch live now!

rules.ruleText: [MDF | Off-Platform Coordination of Re-uploads | Policy Escalation] Handling systematic off-platform campaigns directing users to flood the platform with mirror copies of removed content.

examples: Community post linking to an off-platform drive containing 50 mirror files of removed illegal content with instructions for fans to mass re-upload.

rules.ruleText: [MDF | Crisis & Breaking Events Re-uploads | Elevated Review] Handling re-uploads of graphic or misinformative footage during active crisis events where temporary policy guidance is active.

examples: Re-posting unverified footage of active emergency situation that was removed 2 hours ago for inciting panic during breaking news event.

rules.rationale: Referencing removed topics in metadata without re-uploading violating media is compliant under Section 3.6 & 3.3.
examples: Video Title: 'Why my video on crypto trading was taken down' - talking head video explaining channel updates.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Educational Discussion of Policy | no violation] Commentary on platform policy enforcement mechanisms and transparency reports regarding removed content stats.
rules.rationale: Educational discussions regarding platform enforcement metrics are fully permitted under 1.4 & 3.6.
examples: Podcast episode discussing quarterly platform enforcement reports and transparency metrics for removed spam content.

rules.ruleText: [TR | Re-upload of Financial Scam | Violation] Re-uploading a previously removed cryptocurrency giveaway scam video with altered audio pitch or added borders.
rules.rationale: Direct violation of 3.6 and 3.4. Altering pitch does not exempt content from removal.
examples: Doubling your Bitcoin promo video re-uploaded with audio pitch shifted slightly higher to bypass hash matching.

rules.ruleText: [TR | Re-upload of Harmful Challenge | Violation] Re-uploading a dangerous stunt challenge video previously taken down for severe physical risk.
rules.rationale: Adding a superficial text disclaimer does not cure a 5.4 / 3.6 violation; re-upload warrants removal and Strike 1.
examples: Re-uploading the balcony jumping challenge video with a quick disclaimer added at the beginning.

rules.ruleText: [TR | Bot-driven Re-upload Campaign | Severe Violation] Automated bot accounts mass re-uploading previously removed spam links across hundreds of disposable profiles.
rules.rationale: Violates 3.6 and 3.1. Bot network mass re-upload operations trigger immediate channel termination.
examples: Automated account posting 50 identical shorts containing previously removed fake gift-card site links.

rules.ruleText: [TR | Re-upload of Explicit Sexual Content | Violation] Direct re-upload of content previously removed under Nudity & Sexual Content guidelines.
rules.rationale: Explicit sexual content re-uploads violate 3.6 and 4.2, incurring immediate removal and strike.
examples: Re-upload of explicit adult video clip that was removed yesterday morning.

rules.ruleText: [TR | Re-upload of Cyberbullying/Harassment Campaign | Violation] Re-uploading a targeted harassment video targeting a private individual with added background commentary.
rules.rationale: Re-uploading content targeting private individuals violates 3.6 and 5.3. Harassment of private figures is strictly prohibited.
examples: Re-posting the severe personal attack video targeting a local high school student with background music added.

rules.ruleText: [EDSA | Historical Archive | Permitted] Historical archival video examining censorship history, displaying non-graphic clips of historically banned broadcasts.
rules.rationale: Fully compliant under EDSA 1.3 and 4.5 for historical/documentary educational value.
examples: Documentary on 1970s television censorship showing archived excerpts of banned television broadcasts with historical narration.

rules.ruleText: [EDSA | Press Conference Coverage | Permitted] News broadcast covering a government official commenting on a viral removed video, showing brief sanitized footage.
rules.rationale: Protected under News & Journalism EDSA framework (11.3 & 1.3).
examples: Major news channel reporting on press secretary statements regarding platform content takedowns, with 4-second blurred visual reference.

rules.ruleText: [MDF | Warning Phase Re-upload | Enforcement] Actioning a first-time re-upload violation on a channel with no prior active warnings or strikes.
rules.rationale: Per Section 2.1 & 2.2, first minor re-upload following content removal receives formal warning if no previous strike is active.
examples: First-time re-upload of a minor policy-violating video by a creator who had a previous video removed with warning only.

rules.ruleText: [MDF | Borderline Re-upload Age Restriction | Enforcement] Content containing borderline sensitive material that was previously age-restricted and re-uploaded without age gate.
rules.rationale: Per Section 2.1 & 4.5, apply Age Restriction to ensure viewer safety rather than outright removal if content is borderline permitted.
examples: Re-upload of a heavy stunt video without setting the required 18+ age restriction flag.

rules.ruleText: [MDF | Legal Hold / Court Order Re-upload | Escalation Required] Ticket involving re-upload of content subject to active court injunction or legal hold notice.
rules.rationale: Section 2.3 Escalation Matrix mandates immediate escalation to Legal Team for court order / legal hold cases.
examples: Re-upload of video containing court-ordered privacy redactions that was removed pursuant to valid legal demand.

rules.ruleText: ZERO TOLERANCE: Any photographic, illustrated, animated, or written depiction of child sexual abuse material or sexualized minors.
rules.rationale: Violates Section 4.1.1 zero tolerance rule for CSAM. Preserved evidence, escalated immediately to Child Safety team for NCMEC reporting, and executed immediate account termination per Section 2.2.

rules.ruleText: Grooming behavior or revealing private personal information of a minor in a sexualized or predatory context.
rules.rationale: Violates Section 4.1.1 regarding predatory comment patterns and minor protection. Comment removed immediately and escalated to Child Safety.

rules.ruleText: News reporting or documentary content about child abuse prevention, where no exploitative material is depicted.
rules.rationale: Compliant with Section 4.1.2 and Section 1.3. Genuine journalistic purpose raising public awareness without displaying harmful material.

rules.ruleText: Sharing non-consensual sexual or intimate images/videos of an identifiable individual, regardless of EDSA claims.
rules.rationale: Zero tolerance under Section 8.2 for NCII. Content removed immediately and 1st strike issued. EDSA claims do not apply.

rules.ruleText: Operating a channel primarily dedicated to aggregating or distributing non-consensual intimate media.
rules.rationale: Primary purpose of the channel is NCII distribution. Mandatory channel termination required under Section 8.2.

rules.ruleText: Depiction of explicit sexual acts, penetrative sex, or exposed sexual genitalia. YouTube is not an adult platform.
rules.rationale: Violates Section 4.2 explicit sexual content standard. Video removed and 1st strike issued per Section 2.2.

rules.ruleText: Second violation of explicit adult content within a 90-day window.
rules.rationale: Second violation within 90 days. Applied 2nd strike resulting in a 14-day feature restriction per Section 2.2.

rules.ruleText: Simulated sexual intercourse, erotic fetish displays, or sexual gratification acts without explicit genitalia exposure.
rules.rationale: Simulated sexual acts without exposed genitalia are unsuitable for minors under Section 4.2. Applied Age Restriction (18+).

rules.ruleText: Sexually suggestive thumbnails or metadata featuring close-up sexual poses or fetish themes to game recommendations.
rules.rationale: Violates Section 3.3 (Misleading Metadata) and Section 4.2 (Suggestive Content). Thumbnail/content removed.

rules.ruleText: Nudity depicted in non-sexual contexts such as indigenous customs, nudist lifestyle documentaries, or natural birth.
rules.rationale: Documentary framing confirms non-sexual educational and cultural purpose. Approved under Section 1.3 and Section 4.2.

rules.ruleText: Natural breastfeeding and infant feeding educational videos.
rules.rationale: Breastfeeding in an educational and health context is explicitly permitted under Section 4.2 without age restriction.

rules.ruleText: Clinical or educational discussions on reproductive health, safe sex practices, or sexual anatomy.
rules.rationale: Clinical educational content with clear health utility is fully compliant under Section 4.2 and Section 1.3.

rules.ruleText: Graphic clinical procedures or medical surgical footage involving exposed live genital organs.
rules.rationale: Permitted for medical educational value but requires Age Restriction (18+) due to graphic medical nature per Section 4.2.

rules.ruleText: Classical paintings, nude sculptures, art gallery showcases, or fine art drawing tutorials.
rules.rationale: Artistic exception under Section 1.3 and Section 4.2. Retained with clear artistic framing.

rules.ruleText: Animated, hentai, 3D CGI, or fictional depictions of explicit sexual acts.
rules.rationale: Section 4.2 establishes that live-action explicit standards apply equally to animated and fictional content. Video removed.

rules.ruleText: Soliciting commercial sexual services, prostitution, or embedding links to off-platform adult pornographic sites.
rules.rationale: Violates Section 7 (Regulated Goods & Services) and Section 3.5 (External Links Policy leading to adult content).

rules.ruleText: Standard fitness clothing, swimwear, or lingerie shown in a non-sexualized retail or workout context.
rules.rationale: In scope for review under Section 4.2 but evaluated as non-violating standard athletic attire. Closed with no action.

rules.ruleText: Comedy or satirical performances featuring sexual innuendo or mild double entendres without nudity or explicit acts.
rules.rationale: Protected under Section 11.1 (Satire & Parody). Humorous sexual commentary does not cross into explicit violation.

rules.ruleText: Content that depicts or describes methods of self-harm or suicide in graphic detail or provides step-by-step instructions is strictly prohibited.
rules.rationale: Content provides explicit instructions and graphic descriptions of lethal self-harm methods, posing immediate danger and risk of contagion.

rules.ruleText: Content that romanticizes, glorifies, validates, or encourages suicide or self-harm actions is prohibited.
rules.rationale: Content romanticizes self-injury and explicitly encourages viewers to consider suicide, violating Safe Messaging guidelines.

rules.ruleText: Participation in, promotion of, or instruction for viral challenges/trends that involve intentional self-inflicted physical injury.
rules.rationale: Promotes a viral trend/challenge resulting in self-inflicted physical harm and injury.

rules.ruleText: Content that mocks, ridicules, belittles, or revels in individuals who have died by suicide or attempted self-harm.
rules.rationale: Dehumanizing content that mocks a deceased individual and trivializes suicide.

rules.ruleText: Personal narratives discussing past recovery, therapy, or mental health awareness are allowed if they omit graphic details, explicit methods, and encouragement.
rules.rationale: Educational and recovery-focused content. Includes helpline context and omits any dangerous methods or graphic detail.

rules.ruleText: Documentary or news coverage of suicide/self-harm issues is permitted when framing is objective/journalistic and adheres to Safe Messaging Guidelines, but may require age restriction.
rules.rationale: Genuine journalistic reporting in public interest, but age-restricted to protect younger/vulnerable audiences.

rules.ruleText: When a creator or commenter appears to be in immediate, active danger of committing suicide or severe self-harm (e.g., active livestream), immediate emergency escalation is required.
rules.rationale: Active livestream presenting immediate risk to human life. Escalated to Crisis Response Team for emergency dispatch and immediate stream termination.

rules.ruleText: Livestreamed self-harm or self-injury must be interrupted immediately and the stream terminated.
rules.rationale: Real-time active self-harm on livestream requiring immediate stream interruption, removal, and crisis protocol activation.

rules.ruleText: Labeling content as satire or comedy does not exempt it if the core material glorifies, depicts, or encourages self-harm or suicide.
rules.rationale: Satirical framing cannot shield content that provides actionable self-harm/suicide instructions.

rules.ruleText: Content discussing sadness or psychological distress without mentioning suicide, self-harm methods, or encouragement is non-violating.
rules.rationale: General discussion of emotional distress without any reference to self-harm, suicide, or dangerous acts.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope definition + neutral reference | no violation] Text is IN SCOPE for Eating Disorders review under this sub-category when it makes or discusses claims about caloric restriction, fasting, anorexia nervosa, or extreme body image management. A neutral, academic, clinical, or personal story discussing living with anorexia without promoting restriction tips is NOT a violation.
rules.rationale: Mentioning a medical condition or personal struggle without offering restriction techniques or glorification is allowed under Section 4.4.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Out-of-scope look-alike | no violation] General fitness routines, sensible intermittent fasting for adult wellness, or standard bodybuilding cut diets with safe calorie deficits are OUT OF SCOPE for Eating Disorder violations unless they advocate dangerous restriction (under 500 kcal/day) or pro-ana tricks.
rules.rationale: Standard wellness practices and reasonable fasting routines without harmful tips do not meet the threshold for Eating Disorder promotion under Section 4.4.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope definition + neutral reference | no violation] Content is IN SCOPE for Bulimia & Purging when discussing purging techniques, emetics, laxative abuse, self-induced vomiting, or post-meal burning tricks. Factual medical descriptions of bulimia nervosa side effects (e.g., dental erosion, electrolyte imbalance) with no instructional harm are compliant.
rules.rationale: Clinical and educational descriptions of bulimia and its health consequences serve awareness purposes and are permitted.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope definition + neutral reference | no violation] Content is IN SCOPE for Thinspo/Meanspo when using imagery, text, or audio explicitly designed to induce body shame, encourage rapid weight loss, or idealize emaciated physical forms. Artistic photography focusing on high fashion that does not glorify starvation is out of scope.
rules.rationale: Fashion commentary and runway imagery without pro-ed slogans, emaciated body glorification, or self-harm encouragement are non-violating.

rules.ruleText: [PROH | Instructional Restriction Tips | Violation] Content providing actionable guides, step-by-step instructions, or secret techniques for extreme calorie restriction (e.g. eating under 300 calories/day, chewing ice to suppress hunger, consuming cotton balls) must be removed.
rules.rationale: Providing instructional guidance for severe starvation and concealment tricks directly violates Section 4.4 by facilitating dangerous self-harm behaviors.

rules.ruleText: [PROH | Pro-Ana Community Promotion | Violation + Strike] Content actively promoting pro-anorexia groups, sharing pro-ana hashtags (#proana, #thinspiration, #anamia), or encouraging users to join dangerous fasting challenges.
rules.rationale: Promoting pro-ana groups and encouraging organized eating disorder practices poses significant real-world harm. Requires removal and Strike 1 under Sections 4.4 and 2.2.

rules.ruleText: [PROH | Purging Methods & Emetic Advice | Violation] Content detailing specific methods to induce vomiting silently, recommendations for abusing over-the-counter laxatives, diuretics, or syrup of ipecac for weight loss.
rules.rationale: Instructional guidance on self-induced purging and laxative misuse poses immediate physical health hazards and violates Section 4.4.

rules.ruleText: [PROH | Meanspo & Dehumanizing Shaming | Violation] 'Meanspo' content that uses abusive, insulting, or cruel language targeting the viewer or others to coerce weight loss or enforce severe fasting.
rules.rationale: Meanspo content combines abusive shaming with self-harm encouragement, directly violating Section 4.4 and Section 5.3 (Harassment).

rules.ruleText: [PROH | Extreme Body Image Glorification / Thinspo | Violation] Compilations of visible ribcages, protruding collarbones, and extreme skeletal features captioned with motivational starvation slogans.
rules.rationale: Glorification and romanticization of severe emaciation ('thinspo') promotes disordered eating behaviors and requires removal under Section 4.4.

rules.ruleText: [PROH | Dangerous Starvation Challenges | Violation + Strike] Social media challenges encouraging viewers to fast for extended periods (e.g. 7-day no food challenge, dry fasting) or perform extreme calorie purging.
rules.rationale: Dangerous starvation challenges present severe physical risk (electrolyte collapse, organ damage) and trigger removal plus strike under Sections 4.4, 5.4, and 2.2.

rules.ruleText: [EDSA | Personal Recovery Narrative | Permitted] Personal accounts of recovery from eating disorders, discussing past struggles without sharing actionable restriction tips, purging instructions, or emaciated trigger imagery.
rules.rationale: Recovery narratives that omit instructional tricks and trigger material provide strong support and awareness, qualifying for EDSA under Sections 4.4 and 1.3.

rules.ruleText: [EDSA | Journalistic / Documentary | Permitted with Age-Restriction] Documentary content investigating online pro-ana subcultures, pro-ed forums, or medical treatment facilities. Contains detailed discussion of ED symptoms for journalistic context.
rules.rationale: Legitimate documentary content with strong public interest value (11.3, 1.3). Age-restricted under Section 4.4 to prevent exposure to younger viewers while keeping educational value.

rules.ruleText: [EDSA | Clinical / Medical Awareness | Permitted] Medical professionals or accredited clinical dietitians discussing the symptoms, health complications, and evidence-based treatments for Anorexia, Bulimia, and ARFID.
rules.rationale: Clinical discussions by healthcare professionals fall squarely under Scientific/Educational (EDSA) exceptions under Sections 4.4 and 1.3.

rules.ruleText: [FRAMEWORK | Overlap: Non-suicidal Self-Injury / Imminent Danger | Escalation] Content combining extreme starvation routines with explicit self-harm marks, cutting, or suicidal statements.
rules.rationale: Direct risk of self-harm/imminent danger. Escalate immediately to Crisis Response team under Section 2.3 and 4.3 while removing content.

rules.ruleText: [FRAMEWORK | Overlap: Targeting Minors with ED Content | Egregious Violation] Channels or accounts specifically targeting young teens/minors with pro-ana tips, thinspo, or encouragement to hide eating disorders from parents.
rules.rationale: Stricter standards apply to content endangering minors (4.1, 5.3.2). Requires removal and immediate strike escalation to Policy Specialist.

rules.subCategory: Overlap: Misleading Metadata & Hidden ED Content
rules.ruleText: [FRAMEWORK | Overlap: Misleading Metadata / Hidden Pro-Ana | Violation] Video thumbnail/title claims to be a benign 'Healthy Meal Prep' or 'What I Eat in a Day', but the video contains pro-ana restriction guides and meanspo.
rules.rationale: Combining misleading metadata (Section 3.3) with prohibited eating disorder instruction (Section 4.4) requires removal and warning/strike enforcement.

rules.ruleText: [FRAMEWORK | Enforcement Ladder | Strike 1] Creator had a previous warning for ED restriction tips and uploaded a new video teaching purging methods.
rules.rationale: Second violation following a formal warning triggers Strike 1 (7-day upload restriction, 90-day expiry) per Section 2.2.

rules.ruleText: [FRAMEWORK | Enforcement Ladder | Strike 2] Channel with an active Strike 1 within 90 days uploads content encouraging teens to participate in a 5-day starvation challenge.
rules.rationale: Violation occurring within 90 days of Strike 1 triggers Strike 2 (14-day restriction) under Section 2.2.

rules.ruleText: [FRAMEWORK | Enforcement Ladder | Strike 3 - Channel Termination] Channel receives 3rd ED policy violation within 90 days of prior strikes.
rules.rationale: Third strike within 90 days results in permanent channel termination. Requires Team Lead + Policy Specialist sign-off per Sections 2.2 and 2.3.

rules.ruleText: [FRAMEWORK | Real-Time Moderation | Livestream Interruption] Creator is conducting a live stream demonstrating live purging or taking high doses of laxatives on camera while taking user prompts.
rules.rationale: Violates livestream policy (Section 11.2) and eating disorder policy (Section 4.4). Stream interrupted immediately with feature restriction (loss of live privileges).

rules.ruleText: [PA | Scope: designated terrorist organization | no violation by itself] The post names a designated terrorist organization (the manual's examples are ISIS and Al-Qaeda). Policy 5.1 applies to this group. Check the post against the 5.1.1 removal list. Naming the group alone is not a removal trigger.
rules.rationale: 5.1 applies to designated terrorist organizations. A removal needs one of the 5.1.1 triggers, and a plain mention has none.

rules.subCategory: Violent extremist movements recognized by credible international bodies
rules.ruleText: [PA | Scope: recognized violent extremist movement | no violation by itself] The post names a violent extremist movement recognized by credible international bodies. Policy 5.1 applies to this movement. Check the post against the 5.1.1 removal list. Naming the movement alone is not a removal trigger.
rules.rationale: 5.1 applies to movements recognized by credible international bodies. A removal needs one of the 5.1.1 triggers, and a plain mention has none.

rules.ruleText: [PR | 5.1.1-1 Created by the organization] REMOVE. The content is created by a designated terrorist organization itself.
rules.rationale: 5.1.1 bullet 1 is zero tolerance. 2.2 lists promotion of designated terrorist organizations as an immediate-termination trigger, and 2.1 names terrorist content as a ground for immediate termination.

rules.ruleText: [PR | 5.1.1-1 On behalf of the organization] REMOVE. The content is created on behalf of a designated terrorist organization.
rules.rationale: 5.1.1 bullet 1 is zero tolerance. 2.2 lists promotion of designated terrorist organizations as an immediate-termination trigger, and 2.1 names terrorist content as a ground for immediate termination.

rules.category: Promotion, glorification or celebration of terrorism or mass violence
rules.ruleText: [PR | 5.1.1-2 Promotes] REMOVE. The content promotes acts of terrorism or mass violence.
rules.rationale: Zero tolerance (5.1.1). Removal is the action 2.1 gives for a violating piece of content. The manual does not name a strike for this trigger, so none is set.

rules.subCategory: Clear satire or parody of extremist ideas

rules.subCategory: Satire' label used to shield a 5.1.1 violation
rules.ruleText: [DF | Satire shield] REMOVE. The content is called satire or a joke, but it still promotes, glorifies or celebrates terrorism, recruits, or helps attacks. Remove the label in your mind: if the harmful part would still break 5.1.1 on its own, it is a violation.

rules.subCategory: Breaking news with significant public interest

rules.ruleText: [PA | Target test] Age is a protected attribute (manual note: Including attacks on groups based on generational characteristics). Content is in scope for hate-speech review when it targets older adults (seniors) (e.g., text targeting people as old or elderly (e.g., 'old people', 'the elderly', 'seniors')). If the content does not target a protected group, it is not a hate speech violation and no hate-speech action applies.
rules.rationale: 10.2 first question: if the content does not target a specific protected group, it is not a hate speech violation. If it does, continue to the remaining questions.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-1 Discrimination, segregation or exclusion] REMOVE content that calls for discrimination, segregation or exclusion of older adults (seniors) based on age (e.g., stripping voting, driving, work, healthcare or public-space rights solely because of age).
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists calls for discrimination, segregation or exclusion as removable, and 10.2 says to remove content calling for discrimination against the group. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-2 Dehumanization] REMOVE content that dehumanizes older adults (seniors) by comparing them to animals, insects, disease or subhuman categories (e.g., burdens, parasites, leeches, waste or 'dead weight' that should be removed from society).
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 and 10.2 both say dehumanizing a protected group by comparison to animals, insects, disease or subhuman categories is removed. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-3 Promoting or glorifying violence] REMOVE content that calls for, promotes or glorifies violence against older adults (seniors) based on age.
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists promoting or glorifying violence against protected groups, and 10.2 removes content calling for violence against the group. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-4 Slurs] REMOVE content that uses slurs to attack older adults (seniors) (ageist epithets and derogatory age-group labels used as insults (mild generational banter is below threshold)). If slurs are used analytically or critically, continue to the EDSA and allow rules instead of removing.
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists slurs used to attack protected groups, and 10.2 removes them unless used analytically or critically. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-4 Stereotypes] REMOVE content that uses stereotypes to attack older adults (seniors) (e.g., inherent senility, uselessness, selfishness or obstruction of progress).
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists stereotypes used to attack protected groups as removable. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-4 Conspiracy theories] REMOVE content that uses conspiracy theories to attack older adults (seniors) (e.g., claims that older adults collectively scheme to hoard wealth or sabotage the young). If the content only discusses or analyses such theories, continue to the allow rules instead.
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists conspiracy theories used to attack protected groups, and 10.2 removes demonstrably harmful conspiracy theories about the group unless they are only discussed or analysed. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Satire label used as a shield] REMOVE content about older adults (seniors) that uses a satirical label to shield hate speech. Decision rule: if the harmful element would stand alone as a violation once the satire label is removed, treat it as a violation. Comedy using slurs to demean or promoting hatred is not covered by the 5.2.2 allowance.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-1 Educational discussion] ALLOW educational discussion of hate speech affecting older adults (seniors), including analysis of extremist rhetoric (e.g., ageism research, elder-abuse awareness, intergenerational-equity analysis).
rules.rationale: 5.2.2 allows educational discussions of hate speech, including analysis of extremist rhetoric.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-1 Educational discussion, EDSA] Where educational content about older adults (seniors) would ordinarily violate 5.2.1 on its face (e.g., it quotes hateful material), apply EDSA only if the 1.3 criteria are met: educational primary purpose, critical or informative framing, proportionate use of harmful material, and a public interest that outweighs the harm. rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-2 Documentaries about hate groups] ALLOW documentaries about hate groups or supremacist movements that target older adults (seniors), where the content is clearly critical.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-5 News reporting] ALLOW news reporting that includes hateful statements made by others about older adults (seniors), provided adequate context is given. rules.rationale: 5.2.2 allows news reporting that includes hateful statements by others when adequate context is given, and 11.3 sets the journalism indicators.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-5 News reporting, EDSA] Where news content about older adults (seniors) would ordinarily violate 5.2.1 on its face but meets the 1.3 EDSA criteria and the 11.3 journalism indicators, apply EDSA and document the reasoning in the ticket.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-1 Discrimination, segregation or exclusion] REMOVE content that calls for discrimination, segregation or exclusion of Sikhs based on religion (e.g., calls to ban Sikhs from jobs, services, public spaces or the military, or to expel them).
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists calls for discrimination, segregation or exclusion as removable, and 10.2 says to remove content calling for discrimination against the group. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-2 Dehumanization] REMOVE content that dehumanizes Sikhs by comparing them to animals, insects, disease or subhuman categories (e.g., animal, vermin or disease comparisons for Sikhs).
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 and 10.2 both say dehumanizing a protected group by comparison to animals, insects, disease or subhuman categories is removed. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-3 Promoting or glorifying violence] REMOVE content that calls for, promotes or glorifies violence against Sikhs based on religion.
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists promoting or glorifying violence against protected groups, and 10.2 removes content calling for violence against the group. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-4 Slurs] REMOVE content that uses slurs to attack Sikhs (religious slurs and derogatory labels for believers or non-believers). If slurs are used analytically or critically, continue to the EDSA and allow rules instead of removing.
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists slurs used to attack protected groups, and 10.2 removes them unless used analytically or critically. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-4 Stereotypes] REMOVE content that uses stereotypes to attack Sikhs (e.g., inherent 'terrorist' or separatist tendencies, buffoonery or violence attributed to all Sikhs).
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists stereotypes used to attack protected groups as removable. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-4 Conspiracy theories] REMOVE content that uses conspiracy theories to attack Sikhs (e.g., claims that the whole community is a coordinated separatist or terrorist conspiracy). If the content only discusses or analyses such theories, continue to the allow rules instead.
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists conspiracy theories used to attack protected groups, and 10.2 removes demonstrably harmful conspiracy theories about the group unless they are only discussed or analysed. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-5 Denial or minimization of documented atrocities] REMOVE content that denies or minimizes well-documented mass atrocities against Sikhs (e.g., documented mass-violence events against Sikhs (e.g., the November 1984 anti-Sikh violence as recorded by official inquiries and independent investigations)).
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists denial or minimization of well-documented mass atrocities, and 6.3 points to Section 5.2 for the same content (kept as this single rule). L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-6 Hateful ideologies] REMOVE content promoting white supremacist, Nazi or similar hateful ideologies as directed at Sikhs (here: religious-supremacist or eliminationist ideology (advocating expulsion, forced conversion or killing of the adherents of a faith)).
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists promotion of white supremacist, Nazi or similar hateful ideologies. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Satire label used as a shield] REMOVE content about Sikhs that uses a satirical label to shield hate speech. rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-1 Educational discussion] ALLOW educational discussion of hate speech affecting Sikhs, including analysis of extremist rhetoric (e.g., history of Sikhism, Partition and Punjab history, hate-crime studies).

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-1 Educational discussion, EDSA] Where educational content about Sikhs would ordinarily violate 5.2.1 on its face (e.g., it quotes hateful material), apply EDSA only if the 1.3 criteria are met: educational primary purpose, critical or informative framing, proportionate use of harmful material, and a public interest that outweighs the harm. rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-2 Documentaries about hate groups] ALLOW documentaries about hate groups or supremacist movements that target Sikhs, where the content is clearly critical.
