rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists slurs used to attack protected groups, and 10.2 removes them unless used analytically or critically. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-4 Stereotypes] REMOVE content that uses stereotypes to attack refugees and asylum seekers (e.g., inherent terrorism, ingratitude or criminality attributed to all refugees).
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists stereotypes used to attack protected groups as removable. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-4 Conspiracy theories] REMOVE content that uses conspiracy theories to attack refugees and asylum seekers (e.g., claims that refugee flows are a coordinated plot to destroy a country). If the content only discusses or analyses such theories, continue to the allow rules instead.
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists conspiracy theories used to attack protected groups, and 10.2 removes demonstrably harmful conspiracy theories about the group unless they are only discussed or analysed. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-5 Denial or minimization of documented atrocities] REMOVE content that denies or minimizes well-documented mass atrocities against refugees and asylum seekers (e.g., denial or minimization of documented persecution that produced refugee flows (e.g., the Rohingya)).
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists denial or minimization of well-documented mass atrocities, and 6.3 points to Section 5.2 for the same content (kept as this single rule). L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-6 Hateful ideologies] REMOVE content promoting white supremacist, Nazi or similar hateful ideologies as directed at refugees and asylum seekers (here: nativist eliminationist ideology (advocating forced expulsion, ethnic cleansing or killing of immigrants as a goal)).
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists promotion of white supremacist, Nazi or similar hateful ideologies. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Satire label used as a shield] REMOVE content about refugees and asylum seekers that uses a satirical label to shield hate speech. Decision rule: if the harmful element would stand alone as a violation once the satire label is removed, treat it as a violation. Comedy using slurs to demean or promoting hatred is not covered by the 5.2.2 allowance.
rules.rationale: 11.1 removes content that uses a satirical label to shield hate speech and sets the label-removal test; 5.2.2 only allows comedy that does not promote hatred or use slurs to demean. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-1 Educational discussion] ALLOW educational discussion of hate speech affecting refugees and asylum seekers, including analysis of extremist rhetoric (e.g., refugee history, Convention law, humanitarian-response coverage).
rules.rationale: 5.2.2 allows educational discussions of hate speech, including analysis of extremist rhetoric.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-1 Educational discussion, EDSA] Where educational content about refugees and asylum seekers would ordinarily violate 5.2.1 on its face (e.g., it quotes hateful material), apply EDSA only if the 1.3 criteria are met: educational primary purpose, critical or informative framing, proportionate use of harmful material, and a public interest that outweighs the harm. Document the reasoning in the ticket.
rules.rationale: 1.3 and 10.2 say to apply EDSA and document it when the criteria are met. EDSA Exception Applied needs supervisor approval when L1 proposes it (2.1), so L1 flags to a Team Lead.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-2 Documentaries about hate groups] ALLOW documentaries about hate groups or supremacist movements that target refugees and asylum seekers, where the content is clearly critical.
rules.rationale: 5.2.2 allows documentaries about hate groups or supremacist movements that are clearly critical.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-2 Documentaries, EDSA] Where a clearly critical documentary about hate groups targeting refugees and asylum seekers would ordinarily violate 5.2.1 on its face, apply EDSA only if the 1.3 criteria are met, and document the reasoning in the ticket.
rules.rationale: 1.3 applies EDSA to content that would ordinarily violate but serves a documentary purpose in the public interest. Supervisor approval is needed for L1 proposals (2.1), so L1 flags to a Team Lead.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-3 Comedy and satire] ALLOW comedy and satire involving refugees and asylum seekers (e.g., satire of asylum-process bureaucracy) provided it does not promote hatred or use slurs to demean. Under 11.1, comedy on sensitive topics is allowed if it does not cross into dehumanization or incitement.
rules.rationale: 5.2.2 allows comedy and satire involving protected groups that do not promote hatred or use slurs to demean, and 11.1 allows harsh satire that stays short of dehumanization or incitement.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-4 Policy debate and social commentary] ALLOW policy debates and commentary on social issues involving refugees and asylum seekers (e.g., asylum law, resettlement quotas, camp conditions (policy-level)). Test from 5.2.3: the content discusses relevant political, social or cultural issues and does not target the group for who they are.
rules.rationale: 5.2.2 allows policy debates and commentary on social issues involving protected groups, and 5.2.3 distinguishes targeting a group for who they are from discussing issues.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-5 News reporting] ALLOW news reporting that includes hateful statements made by others about refugees and asylum seekers, provided adequate context is given. Per 11.3 a key indicator of legitimate journalism is that the harmful material is presented as news, with context, and is not glorified or encouraged.
rules.rationale: 5.2.2 allows news reporting that includes hateful statements by others when adequate context is given, and 11.3 sets the journalism indicators.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-5 News reporting, EDSA] Where news content about refugees and asylum seekers would ordinarily violate 5.2.1 on its face but meets the 1.3 EDSA criteria and the 11.3 journalism indicators, apply EDSA and document the reasoning in the ticket.
rules.rationale: 11.3 says the EDSA framework gives strong protection to genuine journalism, and 1.3 requires documenting the reasoning. Supervisor approval is needed for L1 proposals (2.1), so L1 flags to a Team Lead.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-5 News reporting, doubt about journalistic status] When it is in doubt whether content quoting hateful statements about refugees and asylum seekers is genuinely journalistic, age-restrict it rather than remove it.
rules.rationale: 11.3 says to age-restrict rather than remove when in doubt about genuinely journalistic content. L1 flags to L2, who applies Age Restriction.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-5 Breaking news with significant public interest] When news content quoting hateful statements about refugees and asylum seekers involves a breaking news event with significant public interest, escalate to a Policy Specialist (Policy Expert) with EDSA as the expected outcome.
rules.rationale: 11.3 says to escalate to a Policy Specialist when content involves breaking news events with significant public interest, and describes strong EDSA protection for journalism.

rules.ruleText: [PE | Slurs or stereotypes used analytically or reclaimed] Slurs or stereotypes about refugees and asylum seekers used analytically, or reclaimed, and not to demean the group are not removed on that basis. Test from 5.2.3: is the use for the purpose of demeaning, or is it analytical or reclaimed?
rules.rationale: 5.2.3 asks whether slurs or stereotypes are used to demean or are analytical or reclaimed, and 10.2 continues past the slur question when use is analytical or critical.

rules.ruleText: [PA | Target test] Immigration Status is a protected attribute (manual note: Including attacks on documented or undocumented immigrants). Content is in scope for hate-speech review when it targets migrant and guest workers (e.g., text targeting people as migrant or guest workers). If the content does not target a protected group, it is not a hate speech violation and no hate-speech action applies.
rules.rationale: 10.2 first question: if the content does not target a specific protected group, it is not a hate speech violation. If it does, continue to the remaining questions.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-1 Discrimination, segregation or exclusion] REMOVE content that calls for discrimination, segregation or exclusion of migrant and guest workers based on immigration status (e.g., calls to deny labour rights, wages, medical care or housing, or to expel workers collectively).
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists calls for discrimination, segregation or exclusion as removable, and 10.2 says to remove content calling for discrimination against the group. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-2 Dehumanization] REMOVE content that dehumanizes migrant and guest workers by comparing them to animals, insects, disease or subhuman categories (e.g., 'cattle', vermin or disposable-object comparisons).
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 and 10.2 both say dehumanizing a protected group by comparison to animals, insects, disease or subhuman categories is removed. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | HS-3 Promoting or glorifying violence] REMOVE content that calls for, promotes or glorifies violence against migrant and guest workers based on immigration status.
rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists promoting or glorifying violence against protected groups, and 10.2 removes content calling for violence against the group. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

rules.rationale: 5.2.1 lists stereotypes used to attack protected groups as removable. L1 flags to L2, who applies Content Removal.

If the content only discusses or analyses such theories, continue to the allow rules instead.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-2 Documentaries, EDSA] Where a clearly critical documentary about hate groups targeting migrant and guest workers would ordinarily violate 5.2.1 on its face, apply EDSA only if the 1.3 criteria are met, and document the reasoning in the ticket.
rules.rationale: 1.3 applies EDSA to content that would ordinarily violate but serves a documentary purpose in the public interest. Supervisor approval is needed for L1 proposals (2.1), so L1 flags to a Team Lead.

Under 11.1, comedy on sensitive topics is allowed if it does not cross into dehumanization or incitement.
rules.rationale: 5.2.2 allows comedy and satire involving protected groups that do not promote hatred or use slurs to demean, and 11.1 allows harsh satire that stays short of dehumanization or incitement.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-4 Policy debate and social commentary] ALLOW policy debates and commentary on social issues involving migrant and guest workers (e.g., labour-migration policy, minimum-wage and sponsorship-system reform (policy-level)). Test from 5.2.3: the content discusses relevant political, social or cultural issues and does not target the group for who they are.
rules.rationale: 5.2.2 allows policy debates and commentary on social issues involving protected groups, and 5.2.3 distinguishes targeting a group for who they are from discussing issues.

Per 11.3 a key indicator of legitimate journalism is that the harmful material is presented as news, with context, and is not glorified or encouraged.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-5 News reporting, doubt about journalistic status] When it is in doubt whether content quoting hateful statements about migrant and guest workers is genuinely journalistic, age-restrict it rather than remove it.
rules.rationale: 11.3 says to age-restrict rather than remove when in doubt about genuinely journalistic content. L1 flags to L2, who applies Age Restriction.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-5 Breaking news with significant public interest] When news content quoting hateful statements about migrant and guest workers involves a breaking news event with significant public interest, escalate to a Policy Specialist (Policy Expert) with EDSA as the expected outcome.
rules.rationale: 11.3 says to escalate to a Policy Specialist when content involves breaking news events with significant public interest, and describes strong EDSA protection for journalism.

rules.ruleText: [PE | Slurs or stereotypes used analytically or reclaimed] Slurs or stereotypes about migrant and guest workers used analytically, or reclaimed, and not to demean the group are not removed on that basis. Test from 5.2.3: is the use for the purpose of demeaning, or is it analytical or reclaimed?
rules.rationale: 5.2.3 asks whether slurs or stereotypes are used to demean or are analytical or reclaimed, and 10.2 continues past the slur question when use is analytical or critical.

rules.ruleText: [DF | Uncertain] For immigration status-based content, if the 5.2.3 questions cannot be answered (targeting the group versus discussing issues, demeaning versus analytical or reclaimed use of slurs or stereotypes, promoting versus analysing a hateful ideology), escalate to L2 or a Policy Specialist. Never take a final action you are not confident in (10.1 Step 7).
rules.rationale: 5.2.3 and 10.1 Step 7 say to escalate when uncertain. 2.1 describes Limited State / Demotion as the action used for borderline content, applied by L2 or a Policy Specialist, so it is the pending outcome.

rules.subCategory: Ambiguously offensive, below hate speech threshold
rules.ruleText: [DF | Ambiguously offensive] For immigration status-based content that is ambiguously offensive but does not meet the hate speech threshold, consider Limited State. Do not remove without a clear policy basis.
rules.rationale: 10.2 final question: consider Limited State and do not remove without a clear policy basis. Limited State is applied by L2 or a Policy Specialist (2.1), so L1 flags.

rules.ruleText: [DF | Unclear EDSA] For immigration status-based content where it cannot be determined whether it serves a genuine educational, journalistic, documentary or artistic purpose, or the EDSA case is borderline, escalate. Never apply EDSA speculatively.
rules.rationale: 1.3 and 2.3 say to escalate to L2 or a Policy Specialist when EDSA applicability is unclear, and 10.2 says to escalate borderline cases to L2. Limited State is the pending outcome for borderline content (2.1).

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope] Harassment review applies only when the post targets an identifiable individual: someone who is named, tagged, shown, or clearly pointed to. If the post is aimed at nobody in particular, or at a whole group, it is not harassment under 5.3. Example: 'this video is garbage' (no person attacked).
rules.rationale: 5.3 defines harassment as content that targets an identifiable individual. No identifiable person means no harassment violation, so L1 closes it with a reason code (1.4).

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope] Not harassment: ordinary disagreement, or a one-off blunt remark with no malice and no pattern. Example: 'I disagree, your argument is weak.'
rules.rationale: 5.3 covers prolonged or malicious attacks. A single non-malicious comment is neither, and 10.3 separates criticism from harassment, so nothing is actionable.

rules.subCategory: Basis of attack (protected group status, physical traits, personal characteristics)
rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope] The attack must be based on the person's protected group status, physical traits or personal characteristics. Just mentioning one of these, without attacking the person, is not a violation. When an attack is a violation, it is actioned under the Remove rules (5.3.1). Example: 'Love your new haircut, great video.' (mentions a trait, no attack).
rules.rationale: 5.3 names these three bases, and 5.3.1 lists what to remove. A mention with no attack matches no Remove rule, so nothing is actionable. See gap G1 for malicious attacks that match no Remove rule.

rules.subCategory: Extreme insults that dehumanize (appearance or identity)
rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] Remove extreme insults that treat one person as less than human because of how they look or who they are, such as calling them an animal, vermin or filth. This applies to public figures too. Example pattern: 'You are an animal and your face proves it.'
rules.rationale: 5.3.1 lists dehumanizing insults based on appearance or identity, and 10.3 says extreme dehumanizing language is removed even for public figures. L1 flags, L2 confirms and removes.

rules.subCategory: Desire for harm, death or serious injury
rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] Remove content that says or hints that a specific person should be hurt, killed or seriously injured. This applies to everyone, public figures included. Example: 'Someone should run him over.'
rules.rationale: 5.3.1 covers expressed or implied desire for harm, and 10.3 says this is removed regardless of public figure status.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] Remove threats, direct or hinted, against a specific person's physical safety. This applies to public figures too. Example: 'I know where you walk home. Be careful.'
rules.rationale: 5.3.1 says explicit or implicit threats are removed, and 5.3.3 keeps this for public figures. L1 flags, L2 confirms and removes.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] Remove posts that share a person's private information without consent: home address, phone number, workplace or daily routine. For public figures this also covers family members. Example: posting a named person's home address.
rules.rationale: 5.3.1 lists doxxing, 5.3.3 keeps it for public figures, and 10.3 says it applies to everyone. L1 flags, L2 confirms and removes.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] Remove content that shows or simulates violence against a real, identifiable person. The policy example is putting a real person's face on a violent scene. For text, this means a post that describes, links to or shares such an edit.
rules.rationale: 5.3.1 lists content that depicts or simulates violence against an identifiable individual. The manual's example is visual, so the text version is an adaptation (gap G2).

rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] Remove content that tells or urges viewers to harass a specific person, on or off the platform. This applies to everyone, public figures included. Example: 'Everyone go spam her comments until she quits.'
rules.rationale: 5.3.1, 5.3.3 and 10.3 all prohibit encouraging harassment for every subject.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] Remove unwanted sexualization of a real, identifiable person, including non-consensual intimate images or links to them. This applies to public figures too. Example: explicit sexual comments about a named creator under her video.
rules.rationale: 5.3.1 lists unwanted sexualization of an identifiable individual, including non-consensual intimate imagery, and 5.3.3 keeps non-consensual sexual content prohibited for public figures.

rules.subCategory: Mocking or reveling in death or serious injury
rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] Remove content that mocks, jokes about or celebrates the death or serious injury of an identifiable person. Example: 'Glad he's dead, he got what he deserved' about a named person.
rules.rationale: 5.3.1 lists mocking or reveling in the death or serious injury of an identifiable person.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] When the target is under 18, harassment is held to a stricter standard. There is no EDSA exception for direct harassment of a minor. Example: repeated mocking of a named 14-year-old creator's looks.
rules.rationale: 5.3.2 applies stricter enforcement to all harassment of minors and says there is no EDSA exception for direct harassment of a minor.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] Remove at once any content that targets a minor with sexual content.
rules.rationale: 5.3.2 says any content targeting a minor with harassment or sexual content is subject to immediate removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] Remove anything that could help others harass a minor, even if the post itself is not abusive. Example: sharing a minor's school or location.
rules.rationale: 10.3 Q7 says any content that could facilitate harassment of a minor is removed.

rules.ruleText: [PE | Allow] Allow harsh criticism that makes factual claims, even when blunt. Example: 'This reviewer got three facts wrong and never corrected them.'
rules.rationale: 10.3 Q2 says harsh factual criticism is generally allowed.

rules.subCategory: EDSA: educational, documentary or news purpose
rules.ruleText: [PE | EDSA] Content that includes harassing material only to inform, document or teach about it can stay with the EDSA exception, if it frames the material critically, uses as little harmful material as needed, and serves the public interest. This does NOT apply to direct harassment of a minor.
rules.rationale: 1.3 allows the exception when the EDSA criteria are met and 2.1 needs supervisor approval. 5.3.2 rules it out for direct harassment of minors. Document the reasoning in the ticket.

rules.ruleText: [PE | EDSA] If you cannot tell whether an educational, documentary or news purpose is real, do not apply the exception. Escalate.
rules.rationale: 1.3 says never apply EDSA speculatively, and 2.3 says to escalate to L2 or Policy Specialist when unclear. Limited State is the holding action for borderline content (2.1, gap G2).

rules.subCategory: Commentary and criticism in public role
rules.ruleText: [PE | Allow] Allow commentary and criticism of public figures (politicians, celebrities, prominent business figures) about what they do in their public role, even if harsh. Example: 'The minister's housing policy has failed and he should resign.'
rules.rationale: 5.3.3 says commentary and criticism of public figures in their public roles is generally permitted, even if harsh, and 10.3 Q1 gives reduced protection in the public role.

rules.ruleText: [PE | Allow] Allow commentary on a public figure's stated beliefs when it argues against the belief and not against the person's protected attribute. Example: 'Her position on taxes is wrong, here is why.'
rules.rationale: 10.3 Q6 says commentary on a public figure's stated beliefs should be evaluated carefully. Criticizing a belief is not an attack on a protected attribute.

rules.ruleText: [PE | Allow] Allow clearly identified satire or parody of public figures, institutions or ideas, even if harsh. It must not shield a threat, doxxing, hate or harassment (see the strip-the-label rule). Example: a clearly marked parody post mocking a politician's speeches.
rules.rationale: 5.3.3, 10.3 Q2 and 11.1 allow clearly identified satire and parody. 2.3 says to escalate satire of a named public figure, so L1 approves only clear cases (gap G3).

rules.ruleText: [DF | Escalate] If you are not confident about a post, do not take a final action. Escalate. Use this only when no other rule clearly fits.
rules.rationale: 10.1 Step 7 and 1.4 say to escalate when uncertain. Limited State holds the post while L2 or the Policy Expert decides (gap G2).

rules.subCategory: Satire label used as a shield
rules.ruleText: [DF | Remove] Strip-the-label test: if the 'satire' or 'joke' label were removed, would the harmful part still be a violation (threat, doxxing, hate, harassment)? If yes, treat it as a violation and remove it. Example: 'Just joking' written after listing someone's home address.
rules.rationale: 11.1 says content that uses a satirical label to shield threats, hate, doxxing or harassment is removed. 10.3 Q2 only protects satire that is clearly identified.

rules.ruleText: [DF | Escalate] Harassment, satire or parody aimed at a named public figure that you cannot clearly place under Allow or Remove goes to L2, who apply the public figure standard.
rules.rationale: 2.3 says harassment, satire or parody targeting a named public figure is escalated to L2 to apply public figure standards.

rules.ruleText: [Out of scope] The text only mentions or discusses explosives (news, history, fiction, general questions) and gives no instructions for making one. 5.4 does not cover it. Approve. If it does give instructions, use the Remove rule.
rules.rationale: 5.4 covers content that provides instructions or encouragement for activities that could cause serious physical harm. Text that only mentions the topic does not do that, so L1 approves and closes with a reason code (1.4). Text that does give instructions or encouragement is flagged under the Remove rule for the same sub-category.

rules.rationale: 5.4 covers content that provides instructions or encouragement for activities that could cause serious physical harm. Text that only mentions the topic does not do that, so L1 approves and closes with a reason code (1.4). Text that does give instructions or encouragement is flagged under the Remove rule for the same sub-category.

Text that only mentions the topic does not do that, so L1 approves and closes with a reason code (1.4). Text that does give instructions or encouragement is flagged under the Remove rule for the same sub-category.

rules.rationale: 5.4 covers content that provides instructions or encouragement for activities that could cause serious physical harm. Text that only mentions the topic does not do that, so L1 approves and closes with a reason code (1.4). Text that does give instructions or encouragement is flagged under the Remove rule for the same sub-category.

rules.subCategory: Illegal Modifications (e.g., conversion to fully automatic)
rules.ruleText: [Out of scope] The text only mentions firearms or discusses gun laws and gives no step-by-step help to modify a firearm illegally. 5.4 does not cover it. Approve. If it does give steps, use the Remove rule.
rules.rationale: 5.4 covers content that provides instructions or encouragement for activities that could cause serious physical harm. Text that only mentions the topic does not do that, so L1 approves and closes with a reason code (1.4). Text that does give instructions or encouragement is flagged under the Remove rule for the same sub-category.

rules.subCategory: Challenges or Stunts That Could Cause Serious Injury
rules.ruleText: [Out of scope] The text is about an ordinary activity or a joke with no real risk of serious injury, or only says a challenge exists without promoting or daring anyone to do it. 5.4 does not cover it. Approve.
rules.rationale: 5.4 covers content that provides instructions or encouragement for activities that could cause serious physical harm. Text that only mentions the topic does not do that, so L1 approves and closes with a reason code (1.4). Text that does give instructions or encouragement is flagged under the Remove rule for the same sub-category.

rules.subCategory: Challenges or Stunts Targeting Younger Audiences
rules.ruleText: [Out of scope] The text is aimed at children or teens but the activity carries no real risk of serious injury (for example a harmless game). 5.4 does not cover it. Approve.
rules.rationale: 5.4 covers content that provides instructions or encouragement for activities that could cause serious physical harm. Text that only mentions the topic does not do that, so L1 approves and closes with a reason code (1.4). Text that does give instructions or encouragement is flagged under the Remove rule for the same sub-category.

rules.subCategory: Encouraging Viewers to Consume Dangerous Substances
rules.ruleText: [Out of scope] The text only talks about a substance (what it is, its history, its risks) and does not tell or encourage anyone to take it. 5.4 does not cover it. Approve.
rules.rationale: 5.4 covers content that provides instructions or encouragement for activities that could cause serious physical harm. Text that only mentions the topic does not do that, so L1 approves and closes with a reason code (1.4). Text that does give instructions or encouragement is flagged under the Remove rule for the same sub-category.

rules.category: Pranks with Potential for Physical Harm

rules.ruleText: [Escalate] Firearm content where L1 cannot tell if the modification is legal or if it teaches illegal steps, so EDSA cannot be confirmed. Do not apply EDSA on a guess. Escalate to L2 and suggest Limited State.

rules.sectionRef: 5.5 (intro: gangs, cartels, and organized crime groups); 10.1 Step 1

If none is present, take no action.

rules.ruleText: [DF | EDSA uncertain] The text says it is news, a documentary, a crime drama, fiction or academic analysis, but you cannot tell if the purpose is genuine, if the material is framed critically, or if only the needed amount is used. Do not apply EDSA on a guess. Escalate with a Limited State recommendation.
rules.rationale: 1.3 says if uncertain, escalate to L2 or a Policy Specialist and never apply EDSA speculatively. 2.3 lists unclear EDSA applicability for escalation. 2.1 uses Limited State for borderline content.

rules.ruleText: [DF | News about real violence] A news-style text reports real violence by a gang, cartel or organized crime group. It presents the violence as news, adds context and does not glorify it, but you are in doubt. Age-restrict instead of removing and send to L2.
rules.rationale: 2.3 sends content depicting real-world violence in a news context to L2 and says to consider EDSA. 11.3 says to age-restrict rather than remove when in doubt about genuine journalism.

rules.category: Promotion and Glorification of Violent Criminal Organizations and Their Violence
rules.subCategory: Gangs, cartels and organized crime groups
rules.ruleText: [DF | Breaking news] A news-style text is about a breaking news event involving a gang, cartel or organized crime group with significant public interest. Do not take a final action. Escalate to a Policy Specialist with a Limited State recommendation.
rules.rationale: 11.3 says to escalate to a Policy Specialist if the content involves breaking news events with significant public interest. 2.1 lets a Policy Specialist apply Limited State.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope definition + neutral reference | no violation] Text is IN SCOPE for misinformation review under this sub-category when it makes or discusses factual claims about cancer diagnosis, screening or treatment (chemotherapy, radiation, surgery, immunotherapy). A neutral, factual, supportive or everyday reference to this subject with no false or unsupported factual claim that contradicts credible authorities, records or consensus guidance is NOT a violation (examples: survivor stories, questions about a treatment schedule, fundraising for a patient). Move on to the removal gates only when a checkable false claim with demonstrable potential for real-world harm is present.
rules.rationale: Mentioning a subject area is not a violation. Section 6 limits enforcement to false information with meaningful, demonstrable potential for real-world harm, and nothing here meets that threshold. Close with a reason code (1.4, 12.2).

rules.ruleText: [SA | Out-of-scope look-alike | no violation] NOT misinformation for this sub-category: a complaint about a skincare brand's ad, or a fitness video that says 'detox' with no health claim. Also out of scope: opinions, predictions, jokes and value judgments that are not checkable factual claims, and false claims with no demonstrable potential for real-world harm (default M1, M4). Otherwise close with a reason code.
rules.rationale: Section 6 states that not all false or inaccurate information meets the enforcement threshold. Labelling look-alikes correctly prevents over-flagging and keeps enforcement consistent across communities and ideologies (1.4).

rules.ruleText: [PR | MI-1 False cure or reliable alternative to established care | Severity S2] REMOVE content that presents a false or unproven treatment for a serious medical condition as a cure or as a reliable alternative to established care, for example: claims a juice diet, herbal blend or supplement cures cancer or can replace oncology care. Covers explicit assertions, approving restatements and calls to act on the claim. Do NOT remove sourced analysis, debate, criticism or personal accounts that do not assert the false claim as fact (see the PE rules for this sub-category).
rules.rationale: Meets 6.1.1 bullet 1: a false or unproven treatment is promoted as a cure or reliable alternative for a serious condition, contradicting credible health-authority guidance with demonstrable potential for physical harm. The content asserts rather than analyses, so EDSA criteria (1.3) fail and L1 may not close it as No Action. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PR | MI-2 Discouraging life-saving treatment with false claims | Severity S1] REMOVE content that uses false medical claims to discourage life-saving or necessary treatment, for example: urges patients to refuse chemotherapy, radiation or surgery by asserting it is poison or a profit scheme. Covers explicit assertions, approving restatements and calls to act on the claim. Do NOT remove sourced analysis, debate, criticism or personal accounts that do not assert the false claim as fact (see the PE rules for this sub-category).
rules.rationale: Meets 6.1.1 bullet 2: false medical claims are used to steer people away from life-saving care, the highest-harm health-misinformation pattern (physical harm is direct and potentially irreversible). The content asserts rather than analyses, so EDSA criteria (1.3) fail and L1 may not close it as No Action. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PR | MI-4 Dangerous or untested remedy | Severity S1] REMOVE content that promotes a dangerous or untested 'remedy' that could cause physical harm if followed, for example: promotes ingesting a toxic or unproven substance as a tumour treatment. Covers explicit assertions, approving restatements and calls to act on the claim. Do NOT remove sourced analysis, debate, criticism or personal accounts that do not assert the false claim as fact (see the PE rules for this sub-category).
rules.rationale: Meets 6.1.1 bullet 4: following the promoted remedy could cause physical harm. No dosing or preparation detail is needed for the rule to apply; promotion alone is enough. The content asserts rather than analyses, so EDSA criteria (1.3) fail and L1 may not close it as No Action. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Satire or joke label used as a shield | Severity S2] REMOVE content labelled 'satire', 'parody', 'just a joke' or '/s' that is written to be believed and acted on, where the harmful element would stand alone as a violation of MI-1 (claims a juice diet, herbal blend or supplement cures cancer or can replace oncology care) if the label were removed (11.1 decision rule).
rules.rationale: 11.1 decision rule: if the harmful element would stand alone as a violation without the satire label, treat it as a violation. Compare with the satire allow rule in the PE rules. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-1 Educational discussion or debunking | no violation] ALLOW teaching, explaining or fact-checking claims about cancer diagnosis, screening or treatment (chemotherapy, radiation, surgery, immunotherapy) that identifies a claim as false or disputed, cites credible health authorities (WHO, CDC, national health ministries) and does not present the false claim as true. Briefly quoting the claim in order to refute it is fine.
rules.rationale: 1.3; 10.1 Step 5; 6.1 allows this. Educational or corrective framing is expressly allowed. The claim is identified as false or disputed, not endorsed, so the content is not violating on its face and no EDSA exception is needed.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-2 News reporting or documentary with context | no violation] ALLOW news reporting or documentary content about cancer diagnosis, screening or treatment (chemotherapy, radiation, surgery, immunotherapy) that reports on a health claim or controversy with context and sourcing, attributes the claim to its source and does not endorse it.
rules.rationale: 11.3; 1.3; 6.1 allows this. News and documentary content that reports a claim with context and without endorsement is allowed (11.3). Nothing is presented as established fact that is false, so no EDSA exception is needed.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-3 Clearly labelled satire or parody | no violation] ALLOW clearly identified satire or parody touching cancer diagnosis, screening or treatment (chemotherapy, radiation, surgery, immunotherapy) where the joke is evident and, with the satire label removed, no harmful health claim would stand alone as a violation (11.1 strip-the-label test). Does not extend to content that could be believed and acted on.
rules.rationale: 11.1 allows this. Satire is allowed when genuine. The strip-the-label test (11.1) shows no harmful false claim that would violate if the label were removed.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-4 Commentary or criticism grounded in facts | no violation] ALLOW critique of health policy or institutional guidance on cancer diagnosis, screening or treatment (chemotherapy, radiation, surgery, immunotherapy), for example criticism of cancer-drug pricing or of long hospital waiting times, where it rests on factual claims and does not promote clearly dangerous alternatives.
rules.rationale: 6.1.2 (bullet 3) allows this. Criticism and commentary based on factual claims are allowed; only false factual assertions or dangerous alternatives are actionable. Harshness alone is not a violation.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-5 Personal account without categorical claims | no violation] ALLOW personal accounts of medical experience related to cancer diagnosis, screening or treatment (chemotherapy, radiation, surgery, immunotherapy) ('this is what happened to me') that do not make false categorical medical claims and do not advise others to abandon care.
rules.rationale: 6.1.2 (bullet 2) allows this. Personal accounts are allowed when they avoid false categorical claims and advice to others (default M7). Nothing here meets a removal gate.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-6 Genuine scientific debate or emerging research | no violation] ALLOW genuine scientific debate and emerging research on cancer diagnosis, screening or treatment (chemotherapy, radiation, surgery, immunotherapy) that falls within legitimate academic discourse: uncertainty is acknowledged, the work is attributed, and no clearly dangerous alternative is promoted.
rules.rationale: 6.1.2 (bullet 1) allows this. Genuine scientific debate and emerging research within legitimate academic discourse are expressly allowed (6.1.2 bullet 1). Uncertainty is acknowledged and no dangerous alternative is promoted.

rules.ruleText: [PE | Below-threshold falsehood (hard negative) | no violation] ALLOW a false, exaggerated or imprecise remark touching cancer diagnosis, screening or treatment (chemotherapy, radiation, surgery, immunotherapy) that has no demonstrable potential to cause real-world harm and does not tell anyone to skip care, vote wrongly or harass a person, for example: 'berries boost immunity' with no treatment claim (default M1).
rules.rationale: Section 6 limits enforcement to content where harm is demonstrable and significant. A trivial inaccuracy does not meet that bar, and removing it would breach proportionality (1.4).

rules.ruleText: [PE | EDSA-1 Educational or documentary reproduction of the claim | EDSA review] The post reproduces a violating claim about cancer diagnosis, screening or treatment (chemotherapy, radiation, surgery, immunotherapy) (verbatim or at length) inside clear critical, educational, documentary or news framing, for example a debunking explainer that quotes the claim in full. Purpose, context, proportionality and public interest look satisfied under 1.3, but L1 cannot apply EDSA alone (2.1: L1 only with supervisor approval). Do not remove; flag to a Team Lead with the EDSA reasoning documented.
rules.rationale: 1.3 criteria appear met (primary purpose to educate or document, critical framing, proportionality, public interest). 2.1 allows L1 to apply EDSA only with supervisor approval, so the ticket goes to a Team Lead. EDSA is never applied speculatively; reasoning goes in the ticket. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to a Team Lead, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PE | EDSA-2 Journalistic or scholarly quotation with prominent claim wording | EDSA review] Journalistic or scholarly content on cancer diagnosis, screening or treatment (chemotherapy, radiation, surgery, immunotherapy) that places the false claim prominently (headline or pull-quote style) while the surrounding text corrects it. Public interest is clear and the framing is critical, but the minimum-necessary-material test (1.3) is arguable. Do not remove; flag to a Team Lead for the EDSA decision.
rules.rationale: Critical framing and public interest are present, but prominence of the harmful wording tests proportionality (1.3). Supervisor approval is the Team Lead step (2.1). In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to a Team Lead, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PE | Borderline: claim at the edge of consensus, or EDSA uncertain | Limited State] The post makes a health claim about cancer diagnosis, screening or treatment (chemotherapy, radiation, surgery, immunotherapy) that may be emerging, contested or only partly supported (for example: a post says an experimental drug 'seems to shrink tumours' with no source), and L1 cannot confirm whether it contradicts consensus guidance or whether an EDSA purpose applies. Do not remove and do not apply EDSA speculatively (default M2).
rules.rationale: 1.3 and 2.3: if uncertain about EDSA or consensus, escalate to L2 or the Policy Specialist. Limited State is the manual's tool for borderline content (2.1). In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to a Policy Expert, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PE | Borderline: claim status unclear | Limited State] L1 cannot tell whether the claim about cancer diagnosis, screening or treatment (chemotherapy, radiation, surgery, immunotherapy) is false (for example: a post says an experimental drug 'seems to shrink tumours' with no source). The consensus or record is unclear, the wording is hedged or the harm potential is moderate. Do not remove without a clear policy basis; recommend Limited State via L2 (default M2).
rules.rationale: 10.1 Step 7: never take a final action you are not confident in. Limited State keeps borderline content on the platform with reduced reach. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

Otherwise close with a reason code.
rules.rationale: Section 6 states that not all false or inaccurate information meets the enforcement threshold. Labelling look-alikes correctly prevents over-flagging and keeps enforcement consistent across communities and ideologies (1.4).

rules.ruleText: [PR | MI-1 False cure or reliable alternative to established care | Severity S2] REMOVE content that presents a false or unproven treatment for a serious medical condition as a cure or as a reliable alternative to established care, for example: markets a supplement or herbal remedy as a cure for a serious condition. Covers explicit assertions, approving restatements and calls to act on the claim. Do NOT remove sourced analysis, debate, criticism or personal accounts that do not assert the false claim as fact (see the PE rules for this sub-category).
rules.rationale: Meets 6.1.1 bullet 1: a false or unproven treatment is promoted as a cure or reliable alternative for a serious condition, contradicting credible health-authority guidance with demonstrable potential for physical harm. The content asserts rather than analyses, so EDSA criteria (1.3) fail and L1 may not close it as No Action. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PR | MI-4 Dangerous or untested remedy | Severity S1] REMOVE content that promotes a dangerous or untested 'remedy' that could cause physical harm if followed, for example: promotes ingesting or applying a toxic or untested substance as a remedy. Covers explicit assertions, approving restatements and calls to act on the claim. Do NOT remove sourced analysis, debate, criticism or personal accounts that do not assert the false claim as fact (see the PE rules for this sub-category).
rules.rationale: Meets 6.1.1 bullet 4: following the promoted remedy could cause physical harm. No dosing or preparation detail is needed for the rule to apply; promotion alone is enough. The content asserts rather than analyses, so EDSA criteria (1.3) fail and L1 may not close it as No Action. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Satire or joke label used as a shield | Severity S2] REMOVE content labelled 'satire', 'parody', 'just a joke' or '/s' that is written to be believed and acted on, where the harmful element would stand alone as a violation of MI-1 (markets a supplement or herbal remedy as a cure for a serious condition) if the label were removed (11.1 decision rule).
rules.rationale: 11.1 decision rule: if the harmful element would stand alone as a violation without the satire label, treat it as a violation. Compare with the satire allow rule in the PE rules. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-1 Educational discussion or debunking | no violation] ALLOW teaching, explaining or fact-checking claims about supplements, herbal products, detox regimens, home remedies, fasting protocols and wellness products that identifies a claim as false or disputed, cites credible health authorities (WHO, CDC, national health ministries) and does not present the false claim as true. Briefly quoting the claim in order to refute it is fine.
rules.rationale: 1.3; 10.1 Step 5; 6.1 allows this. Educational or corrective framing is expressly allowed. The claim is identified as false or disputed, not endorsed, so the content is not violating on its face and no EDSA exception is needed.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-2 News reporting or documentary with context | no violation] ALLOW news reporting or documentary content about supplements, herbal products, detox regimens, home remedies, fasting protocols and wellness products that reports on a health claim or controversy with context and sourcing, attributes the claim to its source and does not endorse it.
rules.rationale: 11.3; 1.3; 6.1 allows this. News and documentary content that reports a claim with context and without endorsement is allowed (11.3). Nothing is presented as established fact that is false, so no EDSA exception is needed.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-3 Clearly labelled satire or parody | no violation] ALLOW clearly identified satire or parody touching supplements, herbal products, detox regimens, home remedies, fasting protocols and wellness products where the joke is evident and, with the satire label removed, no harmful health claim would stand alone as a violation (11.1 strip-the-label test). Does not extend to content that could be believed and acted on.
rules.rationale: 11.1 allows this. Satire is allowed when genuine. The strip-the-label test (11.1) shows no harmful false claim that would violate if the label were removed.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-4 Commentary or criticism grounded in facts | no violation] ALLOW critique of health policy or institutional guidance on supplements, herbal products, detox regimens, home remedies, fasting protocols and wellness products, for example criticism of how supplements are regulated or labelled, where it rests on factual claims and does not promote clearly dangerous alternatives.
rules.rationale: 6.1.2 (bullet 3) allows this. Criticism and commentary based on factual claims are allowed; only false factual assertions or dangerous alternatives are actionable. Harshness alone is not a violation.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-5 Personal account without categorical claims | no violation] ALLOW personal accounts of medical experience related to supplements, herbal products, detox regimens, home remedies, fasting protocols and wellness products ('this is what happened to me') that do not make false categorical medical claims and do not advise others to abandon care.
rules.rationale: 6.1.2 (bullet 2) allows this. Personal accounts are allowed when they avoid false categorical claims and advice to others (default M7). Nothing here meets a removal gate.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-6 Genuine scientific debate or emerging research | no violation] ALLOW genuine scientific debate and emerging research on supplements, herbal products, detox regimens, home remedies, fasting protocols and wellness products that falls within legitimate academic discourse: uncertainty is acknowledged, the work is attributed, and no clearly dangerous alternative is promoted.
rules.rationale: 6.1.2 (bullet 1) allows this. Genuine scientific debate and emerging research within legitimate academic discourse are expressly allowed (6.1.2 bullet 1). Uncertainty is acknowledged and no dangerous alternative is promoted.

rules.ruleText: [PE | Below-threshold falsehood (hard negative) | no violation] ALLOW a false, exaggerated or imprecise remark touching supplements, herbal products, detox regimens, home remedies, fasting protocols and wellness products that has no demonstrable potential to cause real-world harm and does not tell anyone to skip care, vote wrongly or harass a person, for example: 'this vitamin gives me tons of energy' with no illness claim (default M1).
rules.rationale: Section 6 limits enforcement to content where harm is demonstrable and significant. A trivial inaccuracy does not meet that bar, and removing it would breach proportionality (1.4).

rules.ruleText: [PE | EDSA-1 Educational or documentary reproduction of the claim | EDSA review] The post reproduces a violating claim about supplements, herbal products, detox regimens, home remedies, fasting protocols and wellness products (verbatim or at length) inside clear critical, educational, documentary or news framing, for example a debunking explainer that quotes the claim in full. Purpose, context, proportionality and public interest look satisfied under 1.3, but L1 cannot apply EDSA alone (2.1: L1 only with supervisor approval). Do not remove; flag to a Team Lead with the EDSA reasoning documented.
rules.rationale: 1.3 criteria appear met (primary purpose to educate or document, critical framing, proportionality, public interest). 2.1 allows L1 to apply EDSA only with supervisor approval, so the ticket goes to a Team Lead. EDSA is never applied speculatively; reasoning goes in the ticket. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to a Team Lead, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PE | EDSA-2 Journalistic or scholarly quotation with prominent claim wording | EDSA review] Journalistic or scholarly content on supplements, herbal products, detox regimens, home remedies, fasting protocols and wellness products that places the false claim prominently (headline or pull-quote style) while the surrounding text corrects it. Public interest is clear and the framing is critical, but the minimum-necessary-material test (1.3) is arguable. Do not remove; flag to a Team Lead for the EDSA decision.
rules.rationale: Critical framing and public interest are present, but prominence of the harmful wording tests proportionality (1.3). Supervisor approval is the Team Lead step (2.1). In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to a Team Lead, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PE | Borderline: claim at the edge of consensus, or EDSA uncertain | Limited State] The post makes a health claim about supplements, herbal products, detox regimens, home remedies, fasting protocols and wellness products that may be emerging, contested or only partly supported (for example: claims an herb 'supports recovery' citing one weak study), and L1 cannot confirm whether it contradicts consensus guidance or whether an EDSA purpose applies. rules.rationale: 1.3 and 2.3: if uncertain about EDSA or consensus, escalate to L2 or the Policy Specialist. Limited State is the manual's tool for borderline content (2.1). In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to a Policy Expert, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PE | Borderline: claim status unclear | Limited State] L1 cannot tell whether the claim about supplements, herbal products, detox regimens, home remedies, fasting protocols and wellness products is false (for example: claims an herb 'supports recovery' citing one weak study). The consensus or record is unclear, the wording is hedged or the harm potential is moderate. Do not remove without a clear policy basis; recommend Limited State via L2 (default M2).

rules.ruleText: [DF | Unclear EDSA] For health-misinformation content that reproduces a violating claim and asserts an educational, documentary, scientific, artistic or news purpose, but where purpose, critical framing or proportionality cannot be confirmed: do not apply EDSA speculatively. Flag to a Policy Expert with a recommended Limited State.
rules.rationale: 1.3: if uncertain, escalate to L2 or Policy Specialist and never apply EDSA speculatively. 2.3 lists unclear EDSA applicability as an escalation scenario. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to a Policy Expert, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [DF | Claim status unclear] For health-misinformation content where L1 cannot verify whether the claim is false (no clear authority, record or consensus to compare against), or whether harm potential is demonstrable: do not remove on a hunch. Recommend Limited State via L2 (default M2).
rules.rationale: L1 is not the arbiter of contested facts. 10.1 Step 7 and 1.4: when uncertain, escalate; Limited State is the least restrictive action that addresses borderline content (2.1). In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [DF | Below harm threshold] For health-misinformation content that is false, imprecise or in poor taste but shows no demonstrable potential for physical harm, voter or civic harm, targeted harassment or violence: close with a reason code. Do not remove, restrict or escalate (default M1).
rules.rationale: Section 6 opens by limiting enforcement to harm that is demonstrable and significant. Proportionality (1.4) requires the least restrictive action, and here that is none.

rules.subCategory: Definition met: contradicts consensus and could cause physical harm
rules.ruleText: [DF | Definition met (medical)] Medical misinformation is content that contradicts consensus guidance from credible health authorities (WHO, CDC, national health ministries) in ways that could cause physical harm to individuals. When a post asserts a health claim that contradicts that guidance AND following it could plausibly cause physical harm (skipped treatment, a toxic remedy, an avoidable infection), the definition is met: label Medical Misinformation, select the matching MI-1 to MI-4 rule and remove.
rules.rationale: 6.1 defines the category by two tests together: contradiction of consensus guidance and a plausible physical-harm pathway. Both are present, so the matching 6.1.1 rule applies. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.subCategory: Definition not met: consistent with consensus guidance
rules.ruleText: [DF | Definition not met: consistent with guidance] A health statement that matches current guidance from WHO, CDC or national health ministries is not misinformation, even if blunt, emotional, badly worded or unpopular. Close with a reason code.
rules.rationale: The 6.1 definition requires contradiction of consensus guidance. A statement that agrees with it cannot meet the definition (1.4: apply policy uniformly, not by tone or popularity).

rules.subCategory: Definition not met: contradicts guidance but no plausible physical harm
rules.ruleText: [DF | Definition not met: no physical-harm pathway] A claim that contradicts guidance but cannot plausibly lead to physical harm (a historical error, a trivial wellness myth with no treatment advice, an inaccurate fun fact) is not actionable. Close with a reason code (default M1).
rules.rationale: The 6.1 definition requires that the contradiction could cause physical harm, and Section 6 limits enforcement to demonstrable harm. Proportionality (1.4) points to no action.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope definition + neutral reference | no violation] Text is IN SCOPE for misinformation review under this sub-category when it makes or discusses factual claims about how, when, where and who may vote, including registration, ID rules, mail and early voting and polling-place details. A neutral, factual, supportive or everyday reference to this subject with no false or unsupported factual claim that contradicts credible authorities, records or consensus guidance is NOT a violation (examples: a reminder of the official election date with a source link). Move on to the removal gates only when a checkable false claim with demonstrable potential for real-world harm is present.
rules.rationale: Mentioning a subject area is not a violation. Section 6 limits enforcement to false information with meaningful, demonstrable potential for real-world harm, and nothing here meets that threshold. Close with a reason code (1.4, 12.2).

rules.ruleText: [SA | Out-of-scope look-alike | no violation] NOT misinformation for this sub-category: a complaint about a long polling queue. Also out of scope: opinions, predictions, jokes and value judgments that are not checkable factual claims, and false claims with no demonstrable potential for real-world harm (default M1, M4). Otherwise close with a reason code.
rules.rationale: Section 6 states that not all false or inaccurate information meets the enforcement threshold. Labelling look-alikes correctly prevents over-flagging and keeps enforcement consistent across communities and ideologies (1.4).

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-1 False voting-procedure information | Severity S2] REMOVE content that gives false information about how to vote (wrong dates, wrong polling locations, wrong eligibility requirements), for example: states a wrong election date, polling place, deadline or eligibility rule. Covers explicit assertions, approving restatements and calls to act on the claim. Do NOT remove sourced analysis, debate, criticism or personal accounts that do not assert the false claim as fact (see the PE rules for this sub-category).
rules.rationale: Meets 6.2.1 bullet 1: verifiably wrong procedural information can cause eligible voters to miss or forfeit their vote. The content asserts rather than analyses, so EDSA criteria (1.3) fail and L1 may not close it as No Action. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PR | EL-4 Voter suppression | Severity S2] REMOVE content that directly or indirectly discourages eligible voters from participating through false or misleading claims, for example: tells eligible voters their ballot will not count, or to stay home, because of an invented rule. Covers explicit assertions, approving restatements and calls to act on the claim. Do NOT remove sourced analysis, debate, criticism or personal accounts that do not assert the false claim as fact (see the PE rules for this sub-category).
rules.rationale: Meets 6.2.1 bullet 4: the content uses falsehood to discourage participation. Plain opinion that voting is pointless is not suppression (see look-alike rules). The content asserts rather than analyses, so EDSA criteria (1.3) fail and L1 may not close it as No Action. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.rationale: 6.2.3 says electoral misinformation standards are elevated in these windows. A clear violation is removed as usual; the elevated standard affects borderline handling and priority. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-1 Educational discussion or debunking | no violation] ALLOW civic education and fact-checking about vote counts, certification, recounts, audits and claims of fraud or overturned results that corrects a rumour or explains the real rules, cites the election authority or an official record, and does not present the false claim as true.
rules.rationale: 1.3; 10.1 Step 5; 6.2 allows this. Educational or corrective framing is expressly allowed. The claim is identified as false or disputed, not endorsed, so the content is not violating on its face and no EDSA exception is needed.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-2 News reporting or documentary with context | no violation] ALLOW journalistic or documentary investigation into vote counts, certification, recounts, audits and claims of fraud or overturned results, including alleged irregularities, that presents evidence-based claims, attributes allegations to their source and does not assert unevidenced fraud as fact.
rules.rationale: 6.2.2 (bullet 3); 11.3 allows this. News and documentary content that reports a claim with context and without endorsement is allowed (11.3). Nothing is presented as established fact that is false, so no EDSA exception is needed.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-3 Clearly labelled satire or parody | no violation] ALLOW clearly identified satire or parody touching vote counts, certification, recounts, audits and claims of fraud or overturned results, including harsh satire of candidates and officials, where the joke is evident and, with the label removed, no false voting information or believable fabricated statement would stand alone as a violation (11.1).
rules.rationale: 11.1 allows this. Satire is allowed when genuine. The strip-the-label test (11.1) shows no harmful false claim that would violate if the label were removed.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-4 Commentary or criticism grounded in facts | no violation] ALLOW legitimate political commentary, debate and criticism of officials, candidates and election administration touching vote counts, certification, recounts, audits and claims of fraud or overturned results, for example criticism of a counting delay or of audit procedures, even if harsh, provided it does not assert false voting information or fabricated statements.
rules.rationale: 6.2.2 (bullet 1) allows this. Criticism and commentary based on factual claims are allowed; only false factual assertions or dangerous alternatives are actionable. Harshness alone is not a violation.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-7 Evidence-based analysis of a disputed outcome | no violation] ALLOW analysis of a disputed outcome related to vote counts, certification, recounts, audits and claims of fraud or overturned results that presents evidence and arguments (filings, audit data, counting procedures), even if critical of the official result, and frames conclusions as arguments rather than as established fraud.

rules.ruleText: [PE | Below-threshold falsehood (hard negative) | no violation] ALLOW a false, exaggerated or imprecise remark touching vote counts, certification, recounts, audits and claims of fraud or overturned results that has no demonstrable potential to cause real-world harm and does not tell anyone to skip care, vote wrongly or harass a person, for example: hyperbole such as 'this election is a circus' (default M1).

rules.ruleText: [PE | EDSA-1 Educational or documentary reproduction of the claim | EDSA review] The post reproduces a violating claim about vote counts, certification, recounts, audits and claims of fraud or overturned results (verbatim or at length) inside clear critical, educational, documentary or news framing, for example a documentary segment that sets out alleged fraud claims next to the evidence for and against. rules.subCategory: Definition met: false electoral information with potential to suppress or undermine

When a post asserts such a falsehood AND it could plausibly stop eligible people from voting or erode confidence in a legitimate process by deception, the definition is met: select the matching EL rule and remove.
rules.rationale: 6.2 defines the category by subject (elections, voting, officials, outcomes) plus potential to suppress participation or undermine democratic processes. Both tests are met. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.rationale: The 6.2 definition requires potential to suppress participation or undermine democratic processes. Without it, Section 6 enforcement thresholds are not met.

rules.ruleText: [DF | No credible evidence] A claim that a legitimate result was overturned or fraudulently altered, with no verifiable evidence cited or contradicted by certification, audits or court findings, meets the 'without credible evidence' test (default M3). Covers explicit assertions, approving restatements and calls to act on the claim. Do NOT remove sourced analysis, debate, criticism or personal accounts that do not assert the false claim as fact (see the PE rules for this sub-category).
rules.rationale: Meets the 6.3 Remove test on atrocity denial, which the manual cross-references to Hate Speech (5.2). Applies only where credible judicial, inquiry or historical records exist (default M10). The content asserts rather than analyses, so EDSA criteria (1.3) fail and L1 may not close it as No Action. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.subCategory: Denial or minimization of documented atrocities
rules.ruleText: [PR | Satire or joke label used as a shield | Severity S2] REMOVE content labelled 'satire', 'parody', 'just a joke' or '/s' that is written to be believed and acted on, where the harmful element would stand alone as a violation of CV-2 (says a documented atrocity never happened, was staged or was vastly exaggerated) if the label were removed (11.1 decision rule).
rules.rationale: 11.1 decision rule: if the harmful element would stand alone as a violation without the satire label, treat it as a violation. Compare with the satire allow rule in the PE rules. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.subCategory: Denial or minimization of documented atrocities
rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-1 Educational discussion or debunking | no violation] ALLOW critical, educational analysis of conspiracy theories about genocides, mass killings and other atrocities documented by credible judicial, inquiry or historical records that explains how a theory spreads, why it is false and who it harms, without endorsing it or targeting named individuals.
rules.rationale: 6.3 (Allow bullet 2); 1.3 allows this. Educational or corrective framing is expressly allowed. The claim is identified as false or disputed, not endorsed, so the content is not violating on its face and no EDSA exception is needed.

rules.subCategory: Denial or minimization of documented atrocities
rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-2 News reporting or documentary with context | no violation] ALLOW news reporting or documentary content about conspiracy narratives touching genocides, mass killings and other atrocities documented by credible judicial, inquiry or historical records that describes the narrative, its spread and its consequences with context, does not endorse it and does not name private individuals as culprits.
rules.rationale: 6.3 (Allow bullet 2); 11.3 allows this. News and documentary content that reports a claim with context and without endorsement is allowed (11.3). Nothing is presented as established fact that is false, so no EDSA exception is needed.

rules.subCategory: Denial or minimization of documented atrocities
rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-10 Historical debate with credible sources | no violation] ALLOW historiographical debate on genocides, mass killings and other atrocities documented by credible judicial, inquiry or historical records that engages credible sources, discusses evidence or estimate ranges in good faith and does not deny or trivialize the atrocity or its victims.
rules.rationale: 6.3; 5.2 allows this. Good-faith historical debate using credible sources is not denial or minimization. The trigger is trivialization or denial of documented atrocities, not scholarly disagreement on evidence.

rules.subCategory: Denial or minimization of documented atrocities
rules.ruleText: [PE | Below-threshold falsehood (hard negative) | no violation] ALLOW a false, exaggerated or imprecise remark touching genocides, mass killings and other atrocities documented by credible judicial, inquiry or historical records that has no demonstrable potential to cause real-world harm and does not tell anyone to skip care, vote wrongly or harass a person, for example: a non-minimizing mistake about the date of an event (default M1).
rules.rationale: Section 6 limits enforcement to content where harm is demonstrable and significant. A trivial inaccuracy does not meet that bar, and removing it would breach proportionality (1.4).

rules.subCategory: Denial or minimization of documented atrocities
rules.ruleText: [PE | EDSA-1 Educational or documentary reproduction of the claim | EDSA review] The post reproduces a violating claim about genocides, mass killings and other atrocities documented by credible judicial, inquiry or historical records (verbatim or at length) inside clear critical, educational, documentary or news framing, for example a scholarly breakdown that reproduces the theory's talking points to dissect them. Purpose, context, proportionality and public interest look satisfied under 1.3, but L1 cannot apply EDSA alone (2.1: L1 only with supervisor approval). Do not remove; flag to a Team Lead with the EDSA reasoning documented.
rules.rationale: 1.3 criteria appear met (primary purpose to educate or document, critical framing, proportionality, public interest). 2.1 allows L1 to apply EDSA only with supervisor approval, so the ticket goes to a Team Lead. EDSA is never applied speculatively; reasoning goes in the ticket. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to a Team Lead, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.subCategory: Denial or minimization of documented atrocities
rules.ruleText: [PE | EDSA-2 Journalistic or scholarly quotation with prominent claim wording | EDSA review] Journalistic or scholarly content on genocides, mass killings and other atrocities documented by credible judicial, inquiry or historical records that places the false claim prominently (headline or pull-quote style) while the surrounding text corrects it. Public interest is clear and the framing is critical, but the minimum-necessary-material test (1.3) is arguable. Do not remove; flag to a Team Lead for the EDSA decision.
rules.rationale: Critical framing and public interest are present, but prominence of the harmful wording tests proportionality (1.3). Supervisor approval is the Team Lead step (2.1). In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to a Team Lead, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.subCategory: Denial or minimization of documented atrocities
rules.ruleText: [PE | Borderline: 6.3 threshold cannot be confirmed | Limited State] The post promotes a conspiracy theory about genocides, mass killings and other atrocities documented by credible judicial, inquiry or historical records (for example: questions an exact casualty range in a way that could be read as minimizing) and L1 cannot confirm whether it has been directly linked to real-world violence or threats, or whether it makes demonstrably false claims about a real individual (the 6.3 action threshold). Do not remove without that basis and do not apply EDSA speculatively; flag to a Policy Expert with a recommended Limited State.
rules.rationale: 6.3 sets the action threshold. When it cannot be confirmed, 1.3 and 1.4 say to escalate rather than act unilaterally, and Limited State is the borderline-content action (2.1). In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to a Policy Expert, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.subCategory: Denial or minimization of documented atrocities

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope definition + neutral reference | no violation] Text is IN SCOPE for misinformation review under this sub-category when it makes or discusses factual claims about theories directly tied to real-world violence, threats or harassment campaigns. A neutral, factual, supportive or everyday reference to this subject with no false or unsupported factual claim that contradicts credible authorities, records or consensus guidance is NOT a violation (examples: news analysis of how a narrative led to violence). rules.ruleText: [SA | Out-of-scope look-alike | no violation] NOT misinformation for this sub-category: a game's fictional 'lore' conspiracy. Otherwise close with a reason code.
rules.rationale: Section 6 states that not all false or inaccurate information meets the enforcement threshold. Labelling look-alikes correctly prevents over-flagging and keeps enforcement consistent across communities and ideologies (1.4).
