rules.ruleText: [PR | CV-5 Demonstrably false factual claim about a real individual (defamation or harassment) | Severity S2] REMOVE conspiracy content that makes demonstrably false factual claims about a real, identifiable individual (for example that they committed a crime or hold a hidden role) in a way that amounts to defamation or harassment, for example: asserts as fact that a named private person committed a crime or fraud with no credible evidence, and urges others to confront them. Covers explicit assertions, approving restatements and calls to act on the claim. Do NOT remove sourced analysis, debate, criticism or personal accounts that do not assert the false claim as fact (see the PE rules for this sub-category).
rules.rationale: The 6.3 intro sets the action threshold at demonstrably false claims about real individuals that amount to defamation or harassment. Truthful, documented statements and clearly opinion-based criticism stay allowed. The content asserts rather than analyses, so EDSA criteria (1.3) fail and L1 may not close it as No Action. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [PE | AL-4 Substantiated or opinion-based statement about a real individual | no violation] ALLOW true, documented statements about a named person's conduct (court records, published reports, their own public statements) and clearly opinion-based criticism of them. Truth and opinion are not defamation. Harsh wording alone does not trigger removal.
rules.rationale: The 6.3 threshold requires demonstrably FALSE claims that amount to defamation or harassment. Documented or opinion-based statements fail that test.

rules.ruleText: [DF | Unclear EDSA] For conspiracy-theory content that reproduces a violating claim and asserts an educational, documentary, scientific, artistic or news purpose, but where purpose, critical framing or proportionality cannot be confirmed: do not apply EDSA speculatively. Flag to a Policy Expert with a recommended Limited State.
rules.rationale: 1.3: if uncertain, escalate to L2 or Policy Specialist and never apply EDSA speculatively. 2.3 lists unclear EDSA applicability as an escalation scenario. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to a Policy Expert, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [DF | Claim status unclear] For conspiracy-theory content where L1 cannot verify whether the claim is false (no clear authority, record or consensus to compare against), or whether harm potential is demonstrable: do not remove on a hunch. Recommend Limited State via L2 (default M2).
rules.rationale: L1 is not the arbiter of contested facts. 10.1 Step 7 and 1.4: when uncertain, escalate; Limited State is the least restrictive action that addresses borderline content (2.1). In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.ruleText: [DF | Below harm threshold] For conspiracy-theory content that is false, imprecise or in poor taste but shows no demonstrable potential for physical harm, voter or civic harm, targeted harassment or violence: close with a reason code. Do not remove, restrict or escalate (default M1).
rules.rationale: Section 6 opens by limiting enforcement to harm that is demonstrable and significant. Proportionality (1.4) requires the least restrictive action, and here that is none.

rules.subCategory: Threshold met A: directly linked to real-world violence or threats
rules.ruleText: [DF | Threshold met: violence link] Not all conspiracy theories constitute a violation. The first action threshold is a direct link to real-world violence or threats: the theory has driven attacks, threats or harassment campaigns, or the post urges action against its alleged conspirators. Remove under CV-3; if the link is unclear or the content only uses coded vocabulary, use the Policy Expert rule instead (default M12).
rules.rationale: 6.3 intro: the threshold for action includes a direct link to real-world violence or threats. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.subCategory: Threshold met B: demonstrably false claims about real individuals (defamation or harassment)
rules.ruleText: [DF | Threshold met: defamation or harassment] The second action threshold is demonstrably false claims about real, identifiable individuals that amount to defamation or harassment. Remove under CV-1 or CV-5. Truthful, documented statements and clearly opinion-based criticism are not covered.
rules.rationale: 6.3 intro. Demonstrable falsity plus a defamatory or harassing effect on a real person is the test; harsh opinion is not. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags to L2, who confirms and applies the action.

rules.subCategory: Below threshold: not every conspiracy theory violates policy
rules.ruleText: [DF | Below threshold: no violence link, no individual falsely targeted] A conspiracy theory with no direct link to real-world violence or threats and no demonstrably false claim about a real individual is not a violation, however implausible or unpleasant. Close with a reason code (default M1).
rules.rationale: 6.3 opens by saying not all conspiracy theories constitute a violation and defines the threshold. Content below it is not actionable, and over-enforcement breaches proportionality (1.4).

rules.subCategory: Institution, event or system speculation with no individual targeted
rules.ruleText: [DF | Institutional speculation, no individual] Speculation about institutions, events or systems that names no real individual as a plotter and calls for no action against anyone is allowed. Close with a reason code. If a real person is named as a plotter, use the CV-1 or CV-5 rules.
rules.rationale: 6.3 allows speculative theories about institutions, events or systems provided they do not target specific individuals with false harmful claims.

rules.ruleText: [PA | FW-COMM-1 Licensed Dealer Purchase Scope] Content relating to legal firearm purchases, sales, or transfers conducted exclusively through licensed commercial dealers (FFLs).
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 explicitly permits legal firearm purchases through licensed dealers.

rules.ruleText: [PR | FW-COMM-2 Unlicensed Direct Sales | Severity S2] Promoting, facilitating, or offering direct peer-to-peer firearm sales, trades, or private transfers without a licensed dealer.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 and 3.5 prohibit direct private sales or unmonitored peer-to-peer transactions.

rules.ruleText: [PR | FW-COMM-3 Background Check Bypass Instructions | Severity S1] Step-by-step instructions or methods for bypassing mandatory criminal background checks or legal purchase requirements.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 explicitly mandates removal + strike for instructions bypassing background checks.

rules.ruleText: [PR | FW-COMM-4 Coordinated Evasion Network | Severity S1] Coordinated campaigns or underground networks facilitating illegal firearm acquisition or evading federal oversight.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 and escalation matrix require strike and L2 routing for coordinated purchase evasion.

rules.ruleText: [PR | FW-MOD-1 Auto-Sear / Glock Switch Tutorial | Severity S1] Step-by-step instructions, tutorials, or demonstrations showing how to convert a semi-automatic firearm to fully automatic.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 and 5.4.1 mandate Content Removal + Strike for illegal semi-to-full-auto firearm conversions.

rules.ruleText: [PR | FW-MOD-2 Solvent Trap Suppressor Drilling | Severity S1] Instructional content showing how to drill out or convert fuel filters or 'solvent traps' into unregistered firearm sound suppressors.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 explicitly lists solvent trap suppressor kits under illegal modifications requiring removal and strike.

rules.ruleText: [PE | FW-MOD-3 Mil/LE Automatic Weapon Demo | EDSA] Documentary or police training footage demonstrating standard-issue automatic weapons used by military/law enforcement, framed with educational context.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 & 5.4.2 allow historical, military, or law enforcement demonstrations of automatic weapons under EDSA framework.

rules.ruleText: [PR | FW-3D-1 3D Printed Ghost Gun Files | Severity S1] Providing CAD files, STL download links, or step-by-step 3D printing tutorials for manufacturing untraceable firearms ('ghost guns').
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 explicitly classifies 3D printed untraceable firearms ('ghost guns') as prohibited, requiring Content Removal + Strike.

rules.ruleText: [PR | FW-3D-2 80% Lower Finishing Guide | Severity S1] Step-by-step instructions or jig-milling tutorials to complete an 80% lower receiver into a functional unserialized firearm.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 prohibits instructions for completing untraceable, unserialized firearm receivers.

rules.ruleText: [PE | FW-3D-3 Ghost Gun News Documentary | EDSA] News report or documentary investigating the rise of 3D-printed weapons, showing short non-instructional clips with heavy journalistic commentary.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 & 1.3 permit journalistic and documentary coverage of ghost guns when no functional files or actionable instructions are provided.

rules.ruleText: [PR | FW-MAG-1 High-Capacity Magazine Showcase | Restricted] Content focusing on high-capacity magazines (30+ rounds) without age restriction applied.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 specifies that high-capacity magazine content (30+ rounds) is subject to Age Restriction (18+), not removal.

rules.ruleText: [PE | FW-MAG-2 Standard Capacity Magazine & Optic Review | Allowed] Review or demonstration of standard-capacity magazines (10-15 rounds) and red dot sights for lawful target shooting.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 permits standard firearm accessories and lawful gear reviews.

rules.ruleText: [PE | FW-SAFE-1 Four Universal Safety Rules | Allowed] Educational video teaching the four basic firearm safety rules (muzzle discipline, trigger finger placement, target awareness).
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 & 5.4.2 explicitly allow firearm safety education and legal use.

rules.ruleText: [PE | FW-SAFE-2 Field Stripping & Cleaning Tutorial | Allowed] Step-by-step guide for field stripping, cleaning, and lubricating a legal handgun or rifle.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 explicitly allows firearm maintenance and cleaning tutorials.

rules.ruleText: [PE | FW-SAFE-3 Cable Lock & Gun Safe Installation | Allowed] Instructional guide on installing gun locks, quick-access safes, and safe storage practices to prevent unauthorized access.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 allows and encourages firearm safety and secure storage content.

rules.ruleText: [PE | FW-SPORT-1 Skeet & Trap Competition | Allowed] Video showing competitive clay target shooting at a licensed range.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 explicitly allows sport shooting with legal firearms.

rules.ruleText: [PE | FW-SPORT-2 Legal Hunting Trip | Allowed] Documentary-style video of a licensed hunting trip adhering to state game regulations.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 explicitly permits hunting with legal firearms.

rules.ruleText: [PE | FW-HIST-1 WWII Bolt-Action Rifle History | EDSA] Detailed historical breakdown of WWII bolt-action rifles, mechanisms, and combat history with documentary framing.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 & Section 1.3 allow historical or educational content about weapons under EDSA.

rules.ruleText: [PE | FW-HIST-2 Firearm Legislation Commentary | Allowed] Balanced political commentary or debate discussing gun control legislation, background check bills, or Constitutional law.
rules.rationale: Section 7.1 & 5.2.2 allow policy debates and commentary on public laws and regulations.

rules.ruleText: [DF | FW-DF-1 Satire Strip-the-Label Test | L2 Escalation] Satirical content depicting illegal automatic conversion or ghost gun creation; evaluated via strip-the-label test under Section 11.1.
rules.rationale: Section 11.1 specifies that if the harmful element stands alone as a violation without the satire label, it must be actioned.

rules.ruleText: [DF | FW-DF-2 Live Stream Weapon Violation | Immediate Action] Livestream featuring unedited demonstration of illegal firearm modification or ghost gun assembly in real time.
rules.rationale: Section 11.2 mandates that all community guidelines apply equally to livestreams and should be interrupted immediately.

rules.ruleText: [DF | FW-DF-3 Breaking News Weapon Footage | EDSA Escalation] Eyewitness news footage depicting real-world firearm violence or illicit weapon seizure during a breaking news event.
rules.rationale: Section 11.3 & 1.3 protect genuine journalism with EDSA framework, requiring supervisor approval.

rules.ruleText: [DF | FW-DF-4 Off-Platform Illegal Arms Promotion | Policy Review] Creator with a large platform documented promoting illegal ghost gun sales or trafficking on external forums.
rules.rationale: Section 11.4 and 2.2 extend community guidelines to serious off-platform harm requiring policy review.

rules.ruleText: [DF | FW-DF-5 Crisis Event Misinformation | Escalation] Unverified viral claims about active shooter incidents or firearms confiscation during a declared state of emergency.
rules.rationale: Section 11.5 and 6.2 require strict assessment during crisis periods and escalation to specialists.

rules.ruleText: Remove content providing instructions for manufacturing illegal drugs, including synthesis routes, chemical sourcing, and lab techniques.
rules.rationale: Direct instructions for manufacturing controlled substances present severe physical harm and illegal activity risks.

rules.ruleText: Remove content promoting the sale, illicit trading, or distribution of illegal controlled substances or prescription pharmaceuticals without authorization.
rules.rationale: Facilitates illegal access and commerce of illegal controlled substances.

rules.ruleText: Remove content encouraging illegal drug consumption or portraying illicit substance abuse positively without harm-reduction or educational context.
rules.rationale: Encourages dangerous and illegal substance abuse without any harm-reduction framing.

rules.ruleText: Allow content providing educational guidance on harm reduction and safer practices for controlled substance use to protect public health.
rules.rationale: Meets EDSA criteria; primary intent is public health, harm reduction, and overdose prevention.

rules.ruleText: Allow educational, documentary, scientific, or policy-related content analyzing drug history, mechanics, or legal reform.
rules.rationale: Purely scientific and educational analysis of controlled substance pharmacology.

rules.ruleText: Allow personal accounts of drug use, addiction, and rehabilitation shared within a recovery, therapeutic, or awareness context.
rules.rationale: Personal narrative shared within an addiction recovery and awareness context.

rules.ruleText: Age-restrict content depicting real-world recreational drug consumption that lacks explicit educational framing but does not promote sale/manufacture.
rules.rationale: Depicts legal/recreational drug use without instructional or promotional harm, but unsuitable for minors.

rules.ruleText: Remove content or comments containing external URLs directing users to illicit online darknet markets or illegal pharmacy stores.
rules.rationale: Directs users off-platform to buy illegal goods/unregulated prescription drugs.

rules.ruleText: Live streams depicting active ingestion of life-threatening doses of illegal drugs or dangerous chemical substances must be interrupted immediately.
rules.rationale: Immediate physical threat to life during live broadcast requiring urgent intervention.

rules.ruleText: Escalation required for content discussing substances legal in creator's region (e.g., legal cannabis) but facing strict international restrictions or court orders.
rules.rationale: Complex legal conflict between local legality and international export/import regulations.

rules.ruleText: Content discussing legal alcohol and tobacco products, including product reviews, brewing tutorials, wine tasting, cigar pairing, and cultural/entertainment discussions. Such content is fully permitted on the platform provided it does not target minors, promote illegal sales, or encourage dangerous consumption.
rules.rationale: Compliant content under Section 7.3. Legal discussion, culture, and tasting reviews of alcohol/tobacco products are permitted for general audiences when free from minor-targeted promotion or illegal sales facilitation.

rules.ruleText: Comedy skits, memes, or parody videos featuring adult consumption of legal alcohol or tobacco in social settings, provided the content does not promote illegal underage access, dangerous over-consumption, or non-consensual harm.
rules.rationale: Section 7.3 and Section 11.1 (Satire & Parody). Creative and comedic content around adult drinking or smoking culture is permitted when non-egregious and not targeted at minors.

rules.ruleText: Apply Age-Restriction (18+) to content that heavily features active, intense, or rapid consumption of alcohol (e.g., drinking games, beer bongs, pub crawls) or heavy tobacco/vaping use that could strongly appeal to or influence underage viewers.
rules.rationale: Meets Section 7.3 Age-Restriction criteria. Heavy featuring of rapid alcohol consumption and vape culture poses appeal to minors, requiring 18+ age gating and removal from recommendations while avoiding outright content deletion.

rules.ruleText: Videos demonstrating vape modifications, e-liquid flavor reviews, pipe smoking, or hookah setups without illegal sales links or minor targeting must be Age-Restricted (18+) to prevent minor exposure to nicotine products.
rules.rationale: Section 7.3. Vaping and tobacco device demonstrations contain legal adult material but require strict age gating to shield underage users from nicotine promotion.

rules.ruleText: REMOVE content that promotes, facilitates, or instructs minors (under 18) on how to purchase, obtain, or consume alcohol, tobacco, e-cigarettes, or nicotine products. Also includes marketing alcohol or flavored vape products specifically using child-appealing animation, mascots, or youth-oriented gaming themes.
rules.rationale: Direct violation of Section 7.3 and Child Safety principles (Section 4.1). Facilitating illegal underage access to nicotine or alcohol requires immediate content removal and issuing a formal strike.

rules.ruleText: REMOVE content or comments that facilitate the illegal or unlicensed direct sale, mail-order distribution, or bootleg commerce of alcohol, untaxed cigarettes, illicit cigars, or unregulated liquid nicotine. Includes linking directly to Telegram channels, darknet markets, or illicit e-commerce sites.
rules.rationale: Violates Section 7.3 (Regulated Goods) and Section 3.5 (External Links Policy). Platform prohibits using video or comment space to act as an unlicensed marketplace for tobacco and alcohol.

rules.ruleText: REMOVE content providing step-by-step instructions for distilling illegal moonshine or creating homemade alcohol using dangerous adulterants (e.g., methanol, radiator coils) or producing untaxed, unregulated chemical nicotine blends that present severe health hazards.
rules.rationale: Cross-references Section 7.3, Section 7.2, and Section 5.4 (Harmful/Dangerous Content). Instructing viewers on dangerous home distillation using toxic equipment poses severe physical harm risks (methanol poisoning).

rules.ruleText: REMOVE content promoting or demonstrating life-threatening alcohol challenges, extreme binge drinking stunts, inhaling alcohol vapors, direct eye-chugging, or swallowing tobacco/nicotine pouches in lethal quantities.
rules.rationale: Violates Section 5.4.1 (Dangerous Challenges/Stunts) and Section 7.3. Acute alcohol poisoning and vapor inhalation present immediate life-threatening physical harm risks, overriding general alcohol tolerance.

rules.ruleText: REMOVE content depicting active operation of motor vehicles, machinery, or watercraft while under the influence of alcohol or intoxicated on camera, or encouraging viewers to drive under the influence.
rules.rationale: Cross-policy violation of Section 5.4.1 (Dangerous Behavior) and Section 7.3. Operating a vehicle while intoxicated creates severe real-world harm and imminent safety risks to the public.

rules.subCategory: Addiction Recovery, Harm Reduction & Medical Science
rules.ruleText: Retain content that discusses alcohol dependence, smoking cessation, health risks of tobacco/vaping, or addiction recovery. Even if graphic health consequences or past substance abuse are described, the educational/documentary framing serves a vital public health purpose.
rules.rationale: Satisfies Section 1.3 (EDSA Framework) and Section 11.3 (Journalism/Education). The primary intent is scientific and educational, framed around health awareness and recovery without promoting consumption.

rules.ruleText: Retain historical documentaries or investigative reports covering tobacco industry regulations, Prohibition history, illegal smuggling trade, or liquor tax laws, provided the material presents historical facts critically and does not solicit illegal commerce.
rules.rationale: Meets Section 1.3 EDSA criteria. Historical and investigative context outweighs potential harm, presenting illegal trade from an educational/journalistic perspective.

rules.subCategory: Cross-Border Regulatory Conflicts & Public Figure Violations
rules.ruleText: ESCALATE to L2 / Policy / Legal team when content involves complex cross-border liquor shipping laws, brand sponsorships by major public figures crossing legal jurisdictions, or systematic off-platform illegal alcohol distribution networks.
rules.rationale: Escalation Matrix Section 2.3 (Cross-border legal complexity) & Section 11.4 (Off-Platform Behavior). Complex legal and jurisdictional issues require Policy Specialist and Legal sign-off.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope definition + neutral reference | no violation] Content is IN SCOPE for gambling policy review when it features, discusses, or promotes games of chance, online casinos, sports betting, lotteries, or wagering for monetary/valuable consideration. Neutral coverage, news, or general discussions without illegal promotion or target to minors is NOT a violation.
rules.rationale: Section 7.4 permits general coverage and discussion of legal, regulated gambling. Content contains no links, illegal promotions, or minor targeting.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Out-of-scope look-alike | no violation] Fictional board games involving play money (e.g., Monopoly), video games with purely cosmetic loot boxes that cannot be cashed out for fiat currency, or satirical sketches referencing poker games are OUT OF SCOPE for gambling illegal promotion violations.
rules.rationale: Play money board games do not constitute real-money wagering or regulated gambling under Section 7.4.

rules.ruleText: Content heavily featuring real-money gambling, such as high-stakes casino slot streams, live poker tournaments, or sports betting strategy videos in legal jurisdictions, must be age-restricted to ensure it is not recommended or accessible to minors under 18.
rules.rationale: Per Section 7.4, legal gambling content heavily featuring real-money wagering requires Age Restriction to protect underage audiences (18+).

rules.ruleText: Videos focusing explicitly on sports wagering breakdowns, betting odds analysis, and parlay predictions for licensed sportsbooks must be age-restricted to 18+ to prevent exposure to underage users.
rules.rationale: Section 7.4 allows regulated sports betting content but explicitly prescribes Age Restriction to restrict access from minors.

rules.ruleText: Content that promotes, provides direct referral links to, or demonstrates how to access unlicensed, offshore, or unregulated online gambling platforms is strictly prohibited and subject to immediate removal and a strike.
rules.rationale: Promoting unlicensed online casinos and providing access pathways violates Section 7.4 and Section 3.5 (External Links Policy).

rules.ruleText: Repeat violation or explicit sponsorship driving traffic to illegal or unregulated gambling sites warrants content removal accompanied by a formal 1st Strike against the creator channel.
rules.rationale: Repeat facilitation of illegal gambling platforms warrants a First Strike (7-day channel upload restriction) per Section 2.2 and Section 7.4.

rules.ruleText: Gambling promotions, slot simulations, or skin-gambling sites specifically targeted at children or minors (using cartoon aesthetics, child-directed influencers, or games popular with minors) are strictly prohibited.
rules.rationale: Section 7.4 strictly forbids gambling content targeting minors, intersecting with Child Safety principles in Section 4.1.

rules.ruleText: Operating or directly promoting video game skin-wagering platforms that allow underage players to gamble digital assets for real-world value results in immediate content removal and a formal Strike.
rules.rationale: Facilitating skin gambling targeted at minors represents an egregious breach of Section 7.4 and Section 4.1.

rules.ruleText: Content making false promises of guaranteed gambling wins, selling '100% fixed match results', or offering illegal betting algorithms/exploits that guarantee profit is classified as financial deception and scam content.
rules.rationale: Violates Section 3.4 (Scams & Financially Deceptive Content) and Section 7.4 by defrauding users through gambling scams.

rules.ruleText: Promoting automated casino cheat bots or phishing sites disguised as gambling promo codes is subject to immediate removal and a Strike, with domain blacklisting for external URLs.
rules.rationale: Phishing and malicious cheat links violate Section 3.4.2 and Section 3.5.

rules.ruleText: Live streams featuring active real-money wagering on unlicensed online casinos or displaying illegal gambling promo links in real-time chat must be interrupted immediately.
rules.rationale: Section 11.2 requires live content violating community guidelines (Section 7.4) to be interrupted immediately.

rules.ruleText: Repeat live gambling policy violations warrant a Feature Restriction disabling the channel's ability to host live streams.
rules.rationale: Per Section 11.2, repeat live violations result in feature restrictions (disabling live streaming capabilities).

rules.ruleText: Documentary or investigative journalism content examining illegal gambling rings, gambling addiction, or casino fraud is permitted under the EDSA exception framework, provided it does not promote illegal sites or include active affiliate referral links.
rules.rationale: Meets EDSA criteria (Section 1.3 & 11.3) by providing journalistic context on gambling without facilitating harm or promoting illegal access.

rules.ruleText: Educational discussions, recovery testimonials, and psychological breakdowns of gambling addiction (compulsive gambling) are allowed under EDSA, provided they provide support resources and do not romanticize excessive wagering.
rules.rationale: Educational and recovery awareness content is protected under Section 1.3 and Section 4.3 principles.

rules.ruleText: Content that provides step-by-step instructions, chemical synthesis routes, or precursor sourcing techniques for manufacturing illegal controlled substances is strictly prohibited.
rules.rationale: Direct violation of Section 7.2 (manufacturing instructions for illegal drugs) and Section 5.4.1 (dangerous substances).

rules.ruleText: Promoting the sale, procurement, or distribution of illegal controlled substances or prescription pharmaceuticals without a prescription warrants immediate removal and a Strike.
rules.rationale: Facilitating illegal drug sales violates Section 7.2 and Section 3.5.

rules.ruleText: Content depicting recreational drug consumption that lacks explicit educational or medical framing must be age-restricted to 18+.
rules.rationale: Per Section 7.2, recreational drug depiction requires Age Restriction when not framing manufacturing/sales or harm reduction.

rules.ruleText: Harm reduction content discussing safer usage practices, reagent test kits, overdose prevention (e.g., Naloxone/Narcan usage), or clinical pharmacology education is permitted under EDSA.
rules.rationale: Explicitly permitted under Section 7.2 as public health harm-reduction and scientific education under Section 1.3.

rules.ruleText: Documented off-platform behavior where a prominent creator operates or actively promotes illegal, unlicensed gambling operations or crypto-drainer casinos directly harming users must be escalated for off-platform review.
rules.rationale: Off-platform harmful conduct undermining platform integrity requires escalation under Section 11.4 and Section 2.3.

rules.ruleText: A channel receiving a third strike within a 90-day window due to repeated gambling policy violations (e.g., persistent promotion of illegal casinos) requires channel termination with dual sign-off.
rules.rationale: Per Section 2.2 and Section 2.3, 3rd Strike cases resulting in termination require Team Lead and Policy Specialist sign-off.

rules.ruleText: [SA | Scope Definition + Neutral Reference | No Violation] Content is IN SCOPE for Counterfeit & Fraudulent Goods review when it explicitly references, showcases, offers, or discusses counterfeit consumer products, fake currency, forged government/identity documents, payment fraud tools, stolen financial data, or fraudulent financial schemes. Neutral discussion, consumer awareness videos, educational reviews, or reporting on counterfeiting trends without facilitating sales or distribution is PERMITTED.
rules.rationale: Mentioning or reviewing counterfeit items in an educational/comparative context without providing purchase links, vendor contact details, or promoting illegal trade is compliant under Section 7.5 and 1.3 (EDSA).

rules.ruleText: [SA | Out-of-Scope Look-Alike | Routing Required] OUT OF SCOPE for Counterfeit Goods policy: Unbranded generic items, 'dupes' (affordable alternatives that do not infringe on trademarks/logos), satirical brand parodies without intent to deceive, or general e-commerce complaints. If the content involves financial investment scams or phishing without physical counterfeit products, route to Scams & Financially Deceptive Content (Section 3.4). If it involves impersonating an official brand page, route to Impersonation (Section 3.2).
rules.rationale: Promoting legal alternatives ('dupes') that do not bear fake logos or attempt trademark infringement is lawful commerce commentary and does not violate Section 7.5.

rules.ruleText: [PROH | Direct Sale / Facilitation | Removal] Content that promotes, advertises, sells, or facilitates the purchase of counterfeit luxury goods, knockoff designer apparel, fake watches, or replica footwear. This includes displaying fake products alongside direct purchase links, vendor Telegram/WhatsApp details, discount codes for replica sites, or sourcing contacts.
rules.rationale: Directly facilitating access to and sale of counterfeit trademarked goods violates Section 7.5. Content must be removed to prevent commercial trademark abuse.

rules.ruleText: [PROH | Hazardous Fake Tech | Removal + Warning] Content facilitating the distribution or sale of fake electronic devices (e.g., counterfeit smartphones, fake lithium battery chargers, knockoff power adapters). Counterfeit electronics pose severe physical safety risks (fire/explosion hazards) alongside IP violations.
rules.rationale: Violates Section 7.5 (Counterfeit Goods) and Section 5.4 (Harmful/Dangerous Content due to electrical/fire risk). First offense warrants content removal and a warning notice (Section 2.1).

rules.ruleText: [PROH | Egregious Health Hazard | Removal + Strike] Content offering, promoting, or distributing counterfeit prescription medications, fake Ozempic/insulin pens, counterfeit vaccines, or fraudulent medical devices. Counterfeit pharmaceuticals present severe, immediate physical harm or lethal threats to consumers.
rules.rationale: High-severity violation combining Section 7.5 (Counterfeit Goods) and Section 6.1 (Medical Misinformation/Harm). Poses severe public health hazards, requiring immediate removal and a 1st Strike (Section 2.2).

rules.ruleText: [PROH | Identity Fraud Facilitation | Removal + Strike] Content advertising, selling, or offering step-by-step guidance on creating counterfeit government identity documents, fake passports, fraudulent driver's licenses, fake university degrees, or forged COVID/medical certificates.
rules.rationale: Directly violates Section 7.5 by facilitating document fraud and identity falsification. Requires immediate removal and a 1st Strike.

rules.ruleText: [PROH | Counterfeit Money & Bills | Removal + Strike] Content promoting, selling, or showing how to obtain counterfeit banknotes (USD, EUR, GBP, etc.), fake cashier's checks, or forged financial instruments, including claims of 'grade A prop money' designed to pass pen tests.
rules.rationale: Explicit violation of Section 7.5 (Counterfeit Currency). Poses serious financial fraud risks. Content is removed and 1st Strike is issued.

rules.subCategory: Credit Card Fraud, Carding & Stolen Data
rules.ruleText: [PROH | Financial Crime Tools | Removal + Strike] Content offering, selling, or distributing stolen credit card numbers (dumps/CCs), CVV databases, cloned bank cards, card skimming devices, or tutorials on carding and account takeover fraud.
rules.rationale: Violates Section 7.5 (Financial Crimes/Identity Theft) and Section 8.1 (Doxxing/Financial Data). Causes severe direct monetary harm.

rules.ruleText: [PROH | Refund Fraud & Retail Exploits | Removal] Content instructing viewers on how to execute refund fraud schemes, fake return methods (FTID/Empty Box tricks), or exploit merchant chargeback systems to illegitimately retain goods and money.
rules.rationale: Directly instructs viewers on executing commercial fraud and theft, violating Section 7.5 and Section 3.4.

rules.ruleText: [EDSA | Journalistic Exposure | Exception Applied] Investigative news documentaries exposing organized counterfeit networks, black market currency rings, or identity document forgery, provided the content does not provide actionable buying links, vendor contacts, or operational instructions for replication.
rules.rationale: Clear public interest documentary under Section 1.3 and Section 11.3. Does not facilitate purchase or provide instructions; retained with documentation.

rules.ruleText: [EDSA | Educational Guide | Exception Applied] Educational guides that teach consumers how to spot counterfeit goods, verify security holograms on banknotes, or protect themselves from fraudulent online stores.
rules.rationale: Serves a protective educational function under Section 1.3. Encourages consumer awareness without facilitating illegal sales.

rules.ruleText: [EDSA | Artistic / Film Prop | Exception Applied] Display of movie prop money or non-functional fake documents used strictly in theatrical productions, music videos, or artistic projects, provided they bear clear 'FOR MOTION PICTURE USE ONLY' markings and are not offered for sale as real currency.
rules.rationale: Artistic context under Section 1.3. Prop money is distinctly marked and used for creative filmmaking rather than financial fraud.

rules.ruleText: [MDF | Coordinated Commercial Network | Escalation] Evidence of a coordinated network operating multiple channels/accounts to flood comments, community posts, or videos with links to external illicit replica marketplaces or carding rings.
rules.rationale: Coordinated inauthentic behavior facilitating illegal goods requires immediate escalation to Platform Integrity under Section 2.3 Escalation Matrix.

rules.ruleText: [MDF | Satire Strip-The-Label Test | Removal] Content labeled as 'parody' or 'joke' that nonetheless provides actionable links or contact info to purchase counterfeit currency, fake IDs, or stolen credit cards.
rules.rationale: Applies Section 11.1 decision rule: If the underlying commercial violation stands alone when the satire label is stripped, it must be actioned as a violation.

rules.ruleText: [MDF | Real-time Livestream Sale | Interruption + Feature Restriction] Live streaming broadcast actively showing stocks of counterfeit luxury items, fake IDs, or cloned cards while conducting real-time sales transactions via screen QR codes or live chat.
rules.rationale: Under Section 11.2, active live violations selling illegal goods must be interrupted immediately, accompanied by feature restrictions (disabling livestreaming).

rules.ruleText: [MDF | Account Enforcement Ladder | Termination] Channel receives a third policy strike within a 90-day window for repeatedly promoting counterfeit products and forged identity documents despite previous warnings and strikes.
rules.rationale: Per Section 2.2 Three-Strike System and Section 2.3 Escalation Matrix, 3rd Strike results in channel termination and requires Team Lead + Policy Specialist sign-off.

rules.subCategory: Immediate Termination for Egregious Fraud Ring
rules.ruleText: [MDF | Zero-Tolerance Egregious Fraud | Immediate Termination] Channel created exclusively as a storefront or front organization for severe financial crime operations (e.g., massive fake ID distribution rings, stolen credit card marketplaces, counterfeit prescription drug syndicates).
rules.rationale: Per Section 2.2 Immediate Termination Triggers, channels dedicated to egregious illegal activity or systematic policy abuse are terminated without the 3-strike progression.

rules.category: Home address or precise location data
rules.ruleText: [PA | Scope] IN SCOPE: a home address or precise location data (5.3.1 also names workplace and daily routine). It is doxxing only when this is shown about an identifiable individual without their consent. General talk about this kind of information, with no individual's data shown, is not doxxing.
rules.rationale: The 8.1 definition covers private information of an individual, and 8.1.2 applies to an identifiable individual. A post that identifies no one has nothing to remove, so there is no violation. Close with a reason code (1.4, 12.2).

rules.category: Home address or precise location data
rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] REMOVE a post that shows a home address or precise location data (the manual also names workplace and daily routine) of an identifiable individual without clear consent. Remove immediately.
rules.rationale: 8.1.2: any content with the listed private information about an identifiable individual, without clear consent, gets immediate removal. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags and L2 confirms the removal.

rules.category: Home address or precise location data
rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove + Strike] REMOVE, strike and escalate to the Trust & Safety crisis response team when a post shows a home address or precise location data (the manual also names workplace and daily routine) AND appears to target the individual for harassment or physical harm.
rules.rationale: 8.1.2 (bullet 2): Remove + Strike + escalate to the crisis response team. The manual says 'Strike' without a number, so First Strike is used as the entry action. L1 flags; L2 applies the strike and the Crisis Response Team is told.

rules.ruleText: [PA | Scope] IN SCOPE: a phone number. It is doxxing only when this is shown about an identifiable individual without their consent. General talk about this kind of information, with no individual's data shown, is not doxxing.
rules.rationale: The 8.1 definition covers private information of an individual, and 8.1.2 applies to an identifiable individual. A post that identifies no one has nothing to remove, so there is no violation. Close with a reason code (1.4, 12.2).

rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] REMOVE a post that shows a phone number of an identifiable individual without clear consent. Remove immediately.
rules.rationale: 8.1.2: any content with the listed private information about an identifiable individual, without clear consent, gets immediate removal. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags and L2 confirms the removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove + Strike] REMOVE, strike and escalate to the Trust & Safety crisis response team when a post shows a phone number AND appears to target the individual for harassment or physical harm.
rules.rationale: 8.1.2 (bullet 2): Remove + Strike + escalate to the crisis response team. The manual says 'Strike' without a number, so First Strike is used as the entry action. L1 flags; L2 applies the strike and the Crisis Response Team is told.

rules.category: Email addresses not published publicly by the individual themselves
rules.ruleText: [PA | Scope] IN SCOPE: an email address that the individual has not published publicly themselves. It is doxxing only when this is shown about an identifiable individual without their consent. General talk about this kind of information, with no individual's data shown, is not doxxing.
rules.rationale: The 8.1 definition covers private information of an individual, and 8.1.2 applies to an identifiable individual. A post that identifies no one has nothing to remove, so there is no violation. Close with a reason code (1.4, 12.2).

rules.category: Email addresses not published publicly by the individual themselves
rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] REMOVE a post that shows an email address that the individual has not published publicly themselves of an identifiable individual without clear consent. Remove immediately.
rules.rationale: 8.1.2: any content with the listed private information about an identifiable individual, without clear consent, gets immediate removal. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags and L2 confirms the removal.

rules.category: Email addresses not published publicly by the individual themselves
rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove + Strike] REMOVE, strike and escalate to the Trust & Safety crisis response team when a post shows an email address that the individual has not published publicly themselves AND appears to target the individual for harassment or physical harm.
rules.rationale: 8.1.2 (bullet 2): Remove + Strike + escalate to the crisis response team. The manual says 'Strike' without a number, so First Strike is used as the entry action. L1 flags; L2 applies the strike and the Crisis Response Team is told.

rules.category: Financial information (bank accounts, credit card numbers)
rules.ruleText: [PA | Scope] IN SCOPE: financial information, such as a bank account or credit card number. It is doxxing only when this is shown about an identifiable individual without their consent. General talk about this kind of information, with no individual's data shown, is not doxxing.
rules.rationale: The 8.1 definition covers private information of an individual, and 8.1.2 applies to an identifiable individual. A post that identifies no one has nothing to remove, so there is no violation. Close with a reason code (1.4, 12.2).

rules.category: Financial information (bank accounts, credit card numbers)
rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] REMOVE a post that shows financial information, such as a bank account or credit card number of an identifiable individual without clear consent. Remove immediately.
rules.rationale: 8.1.2: any content with the listed private information about an identifiable individual, without clear consent, gets immediate removal. In this phase L1 only approves or flags, so L1 flags and L2 confirms the removal.

rules.category: Financial information (bank accounts, credit card numbers)
rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove + Strike] REMOVE, strike and escalate to the Trust & Safety crisis response team when a post shows financial information, such as a bank account or credit card number AND appears to target the individual for harassment or physical harm.
rules.rationale: 8.1.2 (bullet 2): Remove + Strike + escalate to the crisis response team. The manual says 'Strike' without a number, so First Strike is used as the entry action. L1 flags; L2 applies the strike and the Crisis Response Team is told.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Immediate Termination] ESCALATE FOR TERMINATION when doxxing content directly endangers a specific individual's safety. No strike steps are needed.
rules.rationale: 2.2 lists doxxing that directly endangers a specific individual's safety as an immediate termination trigger with no strike required. 2.1 requires Team Lead / Policy Specialist for this action, so L1 flags to both.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] REMOVE a post that collects details that are each public (for example a public social media handle, a public professional title, a public business address) and uses them to help harass the individual.
rules.rationale: 8.1.3 says public information is still a violation when it is aggregated and weaponized to facilitate harassment. L1 flags and L2 confirms the removal.

rules.ruleText: [PR | Remove] REMOVE a post that uses a satire or parody label to shield doxxing. Test: if the private information would still be a violation with the label removed, treat it as a violation.
rules.rationale: 11.1 names doxxing as content a satirical label cannot shield, and its decision rule removes the label to judge the harm. L1 flags and L2 confirms the removal.

rules.category: Email addresses not published publicly by the individual themselves
rules.ruleText: [PE | Allow] ALLOW an email address that the individual has published publicly themselves. 8.1.1 only protects addresses 'not published publicly by the individual themselves'.
rules.rationale: The manual's own wording for this category limits it to addresses the individual has not published. A self-published address is not private under 8.1.3, so no violation.

rules.category: Sexual orientation or gender identity if the person has not publicly disclosed this
rules.ruleText: [PE | Allow] ALLOW a reference to a person's sexual orientation or gender identity when the person has publicly disclosed it themselves. 8.1.1 only protects it 'if the person has not publicly disclosed this'.
rules.rationale: The manual's own wording for this category limits it to information the person has not made public. A publicly disclosed identity is not private under 8.1.3, so no violation.

rules.ruleText: [PE | Allow] ALLOW when the individual gave clear consent, or made the information public themselves (for example a public social media handle, a public professional title, a public business address). This is not treated as private information.
rules.rationale: 8.1.2 removes only content shared 'without clear consent', and 8.1.3 says information voluntarily and publicly disclosed by the individual is not private. No violation. If the details are being collected to harass, see DX-ALL-PR-02.

rules.ruleText: [DF | Public figure] Doxxing applies to all individuals, including public figures. Criticism, satire and parody of a public figure's public role are allowed, but a post that reveals private information about them (for example a home address or family members) must be removed.
rules.rationale: 10.3 (Q4) says to remove content that reveals private information about the subject, and that doxxing applies to public figures too. 5.3.3 lists home address and family members as still prohibited. 2.3 sends public-figure content to L2, so L1 flags to L2.

rules.ruleText: [DF | Uncertain] If you are not confident whether the information is private or public, or whether the individual agreed, do not take a final action. Escalate. The post stays in Limited State until L2 decides.
rules.rationale: 10.1 (Step 7) and 1.4: when uncertain, escalate and never take a final action you are not confident in. 2.1 uses Limited State for borderline content.

rules.subCategory: Content ID claims and DMCA takedowns
rules.ruleText: [HC | Content ID & DMCA] Community Guidelines moderators do not decide who owns copyrighted content. Copyright claims go through the Content ID system and the DMCA process. L1 takes no moderation action on the ownership question.
rules.rationale: 9.1: moderators do not adjudicate copyright ownership, and claims are handled through Content ID and the DMCA process. Nothing for L1 to action.

rules.ruleText: [HC | Legal team] When a creator submits a counter-notification to a copyright takedown, it is a legal process handled by the Legal team, not by the moderation team. L1 takes no moderation action.
rules.rationale: 9.1: counter-notification is a legal process owned by the Legal team, not the moderation team. It is not listed as a moderator escalation in 9.2 (open point P3).

rules.category: Copyrighted Material with a Community Guidelines Violation
rules.subCategory: Copyrighted material together with a Community Guidelines violation
rules.ruleText: [PR | Copyright plus Guidelines violation] If content appears to include copyrighted material together with a Community Guidelines violation (the manual's example: pirated content used to spread hate speech), action the Community Guidelines violation and note the copyright concern in the ticket.
rules.rationale: 9.1: action the Community Guidelines violation and note the copyright concern. The exact action follows the other policy that is violated; Content Removal is a stand-in for it (open point P2). L2 confirms (2.1).

rules.subCategory: Repeated false copyright claims used to harass creators
rules.ruleText: [PR | Copyright Harassment] Escalate to the Copyright Team when a creator is filing repeated false copyright claims as a harassment tool against other creators.
rules.rationale: 9.2 names Copyright Harassment as a Copyright Team escalation. The manual says only 'escalate' and gives no enforcement action. Limited State / Demotion is a placeholder for the interim state while the Copyright Team decides (open point P1).

rules.ruleText: [PR | Systematic piracy] Escalate to the Copyright Team when content appears to be a systematic piracy operation.
rules.rationale: 9.2 lists a systematic piracy operation as a Copyright Team escalation. The manual says only 'escalate' and gives no enforcement action. Limited State / Demotion is a placeholder for the interim state while the Copyright Team decides (open point P1).

rules.subCategory: Defamatory claims inside a copyright dispute
rules.ruleText: [PR | Defamatory claims] Escalate to the Copyright Team when a copyright dispute involves potentially defamatory claims.
rules.rationale: 9.2 lists copyright disputes with potentially defamatory claims as a Copyright Team escalation. The manual says only 'escalate' and gives no enforcement action. Limited State / Demotion is a placeholder for the interim state while the Copyright Team decides (open point P1).
